papers.title_en: Data augmentation by an electro-vibratory feedback improves signal interpretation by neural networks
papers.abstract_en: Data-driven machine learning algorithms represent an alternative to numerical or analytical modeling of vibrating objects for the purpose of extracting their material or geometric properties. Their performance is conditioned by the quality of the training dataset, which should contain all possible production configurations of the object and measurement conditions. In this work, we propose a data-augmentation method based on manipulations of the vibration properties rather than numerical signal post-processing. Instead of modifying the sample’s material or geometry, we connect an additional sensor and actuator to the sample and use low-latency electronics to control the feedback signal. This delivers an electromechanical system with tunable oscillation properties. This signal diversification method is demonstrated on the classification of correct and incorrect adhesion of two aluminum plates. The labeling accuracy of 67% on nine unknown test objects, when trained on a single unchangeable training object, increases to 83% when the variety of the training vibration signals is augmented by varying the parameters of the electrovibratory feedback. This provides advantages for industrial quality control, where a large number of reference training samples are not available.

papers.title_en: u-d Quark Matter in the Enhanced pQCD Model and u-d Quark Stars in Gravity’s Rainbow
The Search for Mev-scale Neutrinos in Temporal Coincidence With o4 Gravitational Wave Events Using the Sno+ Experiment
papers.abstract_en: This dissertation presents a search for low-energy neutrinos in temporal coincidence with gravitational wave events reported by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration during the fourth observing run (O4), using 499.0 days of data collected during the liquid scintillator phase of the SNO+ experiment. The search uses inverse beta decay (IBD), which is primarily sensitive to electron antineutrinos, and neutrino-proton elastic scattering, a complementary neutral current channel providing sensitivity to all neutrino flavors. Candidate events were identified using optimized reconstruction and event-selection criteria developed with Monte Carlo simulations and validated with background-only data. The IBD background rate was measured directly from data, naturally incorporating reactor antineutrinos, geoneutrinos, radioactive backgrounds, cosmogenic backgrounds, and accidental coincidences present during detector operation. A model-independent framework was developed using flat spectrum neutrino Monte Carlo samples, allowing the detector response to be evaluated as a function of neutrino energy and applied to different theoretical emission models. As part of this work, improvements were made to the SNO+ Monte Carlo simulation, including modifications to the IBD generator to produce a true flat neutrino spectrum and corrections to the implementation of the neutrino-proton elastic scattering cross section. Detector characterization studies, including measurements of the deployed scintillator light yield and investigations of detector timing and electronics performance, were also performed to validate the detector response used throughout the analysis. The final gravitational wave-coincident dataset contained 143 candidates overlapping stable SNO+ data-taking periods. After excluding candidates classified as terrestrial or unknown by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration, the final astrophysical sample used for compact binary merger fluence limits contained 126 gravitational wave candidates. No statistically significant neutrino excess was observed in either the IBD or neutrino-proton elastic scattering channels. The IBD search observed no coincident candidates in the final astrophysical gravitational wave sample, consistent with an expected background of 1.25 ± 0.09 events. The corresponding Feldman-Cousins 90% confidence level upper limit is N90stack = 1.47 signal events. Stacked average (per gravitational wave) upper limits on the electron antineutrino fluence were derived for both monoenergetic neutrino emission and model-dependent spectra, including thermal neutrino and core-collapse supernova-inspired models used as detector sensitivity benchmarks. The neutrino-proton elastic scattering search represents the first application of this all-flavor channel to a gravitational wave-coincident neutrino search. Using an optimized ±50 s coincidence window, 108424 candidate events were observed, consistent with the expected background of 108345 ± 786 events estimated from local sidebands. The observed 0.24σ fluctuation is consistent with the background-only hypothesis. For the final astrophysical gravitational wave sample, the Feldman-Cousins method gives a 90% confidence level upper limit of N90stack = 1479.6 signal events. These results are used to derive the first all-flavor neutrino-proton elastic scattering fluence limits associated with compact binary merger candidates. The resulting SNO+ IBD fluence limits improve upon previous liquid scintillator gravitational wave-neutrino searches by approximately an order of magnitude in the few-MeV energy region, primarily due to the larger fiducial target mass, increased gravitational wave sample size, and low background rate achieved in SNO+. The neutrino-proton elastic scattering results establish the first all-flavor MeV neutrino search through this interaction channel in coincidence with gravitational wave events. Together, these analyses extend previous multi-messenger searches performed by Borexino, KamLAND, and Super-Kamiokande and demonstrate the capability of SNO+ to search for weak neutrino signals associated with astrophysical transients.

papers.title_en:
Scale Up in Length of Nb
                    <sub>3</sub>
                    Sn Accelerator Magnets: The Experience From MQXF Coils
papers.abstract_en: Future high-energy proton colliders will require high-field accelerator magnets that exceed the capabilities of Nb-Ti technology. The Nb₃Sn quadrupole magnets developed for the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) upgrade represent the first large-scale application of this technology in an operational accelerator. Following an extensive short-model R&D program comprising approximately 40 coils and seven 1.5 m-long magnets, a full-scale prototyping phase established the foundation for series production. The series-fabrication phase is now approaching completion, with more than 120 coils of 4.5 m length produced by the US Accelerator Upgrade Project and more than 70 coils of 7.2 m length manufactured at CERN. This large-scale effort, distributed across multiple manufacturing sites, provides a unique opportunity to assess the scalability of Nb₃Sn technology in terms of magnet length, production volume, and manufacturing throughput. We present an overview of the production timeline, learning curve, major nonconformities, and process improvements, with a particular focus on coil fabrication.

papers.title_en: ESC Enables Protection of an Accelerator Superconducting Magnet With $>$5 kA/mm$^{2}$ Copper Current Density
papers.abstract_en: A new quench-protection technique, energy shift with coupling (ESC), has recently been proposed and shows significant promise for the protection of high-field magnets. The ESC system includes normal-conducting coils that are strongly magnetically coupled to, but galvanically insulated from, the magnet coils. When activated, the system rapidly transfers energy from the magnet to the ESC coils, substantially reducing ohmic losses at the magnet hot spot and promoting the transition of the superconducting coils to the normal state through transient losses. During the subsequent magnet-current discharge, part of the stored magnetic energy is transferred to the ESC coils. ESC was recently demonstrated successfully at CERN on a 400 mm long flat racetrack magnet structure without an aperture. In this work, we present the application of the ESC method to a subscale common-coil magnet known as the subscale stress-managed common-coil series (subSMCC2), designed and manufactured by the Magnet Development Laboratory at the Paul Scherrer Institute. The subSMCC2 is a 300 mm long magnet comprising four stress-managed Nb₃Sn common coils and is designed to reach bore and peak coil fields of approximately 5.3 T and 6.4 T, respectively, at a short-sample current of 9.5 kA. Protecting this magnet following a quench, without the use of energy extraction, is particularly challenging because of its very high stabilizer current density, exceeding 5 kA/mm². The proposed ESC-based protection scheme employs two common-coil-type ESC coils made from rectangular copper conductors and located on the outer sides of the magnet coils. Tests performed at the CERN magnet test facility successfully demonstrated the performance of the ESC system under a variety of operating conditions. These results show that ESC is an effective, high-performance quench-protection technology capable of protecting magnets operating at very high current densities.

papers.title_en: Quantum Key Distribution Network Simulator With Hyperparameter Tuning for Realistic Performance Analysis
papers.abstract_en: Realistic simulation of quantum key distribution (QKD) networks requires a combination of precise models of quantum channels and network functions. Unfortunately, existing QKD network simulators lack either rigorous quantum physics modeling or network key-management and routing protocols, which limit their practical applicability. To address this limitation, we propose a QKD network simulator with hyperparameter tuning (QKDSim-HT), a NetSquid-based simulator specialized for polarization-based discrete-variable QKD networks. Specifically, QKDSim-HT models properties in quantum physics (photon loss, polarization-dependent depolarization, detector inefficiencies, dark counts, and dead times) as well as advanced functionalities in networking algorithms (multi-hop key relay and adaptive routing). Extensive simulations over diverse topologies reveal that the networking performance varied with respect to the fundamental properties of quantum physics, such as depolarization, fiber length, and channel attenuation. As a representative use case of QKDSim-HT, simulation results from QKDSim-HT over simple examples clearly manifest that a design of QKD networks highly affects performance of the networks. Accordingly, QKDSim-HT can serve as a practical platform for performance evaluation and optimization of quantum secured network.

papers.title_en: Suppression of two-stream and Weibel instabilities in ultra-relativistic electron–positron plasma
papers.abstract_en: We present a unified theoretical framework for analyzing both electrostatic two-stream and electromagnetic Weibel instabilities in counterstreaming electron-positron pair plasmas. Through systematic derivation of dispersion relations in non-relativistic and relativistic regimes, we demonstrate how the symmetric mass ratio fundamentally alters instability characteristics compared to electron-ion systems. The two-stream instability, driven by longitudinal electrostatic perturbations parallel to beam motion, exhibits enhanced growth rates in pair plasmas due to equal contributions from both species, with relativistic suppression scaling as γ0−3 for both electrons and positrons. The Weibel instability, arising from transverse electromagnetic modes perpendicular to streaming directions, lacks the heavy-ion stabilization present in electron-ion plasmas, producing broader unstable spectral ranges and modified saturation levels. We derive explicit conditions determining the relative dominance of each mechanism across parameter space defined by drift velocity, wavenumber orientation, and relativistic Lorentz factor. Our analysis shows that longitudinal two-stream modes dominate at small perpendicular wavenumbers and moderate drift velocities, while transverse Weibel modes become prevalent at high perpendicular wavenumbers and large velocity spreads or temperature anisotropies. These findings have direct implications for understanding magnetic field generation, particle acceleration, and energy dissipation in astrophysical pair plasmas including pulsar wind nebulae, gamma-ray burst internal shocks, and active galactic nuclei jets where counterstreaming pair populations naturally arise.

papers.title_en: Developing and validating models of open quantum systems in solid-state nanostructures
papers.abstract_en: Realistic quantum devices are open systems, and their behaviour depends not only on the subsystem of interest but also on how the environment is modelled and how the relevant observables are extracted. This thesis studies that problem in three settings. First, we study cavity-assisted qubit readout beyond the dispersive regime. We show that once coherent excitation exchange and dissipation become relevant, a microscopic treatment is needed to describe the readout quantitatively, and the optimal readout is set by a trade-off between signal accumulation and the distinguishability of the readout states. Second, we compare fermionic and spin baths in non-interacting transport models and show that spin baths reproduce fermionic reduced dynamics only in the large-bath weak-coupling limit, while clear deviations appear for smaller baths and near half-filling. Third, we study charge transport in molecular junctions using Automated Compression of Environments (ACE). There, the main difficulty is not the time evolution itself, but the extraction of the transport current, since this observable depends on system-environment correlations and is therefore not contained in the reduced system density matrix alone. We show that a probe-mode construction provides a viable route to reformulate the current as a system observable. This thesis advances our understanding of what is required for accurate modelling of open quantum dynamics across a range of solid-state settings, from cavity-assisted qubit readout to charge transport in molecular junctions.

papers.title_en: Using Printed Circuit Boards and MOSFET Switch Arrays Toward the Reliable Manufacture of Superconducting Rectifiers
papers.abstract_en: Using superconducting rectifiers to energize high-temperature superconducting (HTS) magnets is a promising approach to accelerate the uptake of HTS magnet technology. In this work, we start to address two limitations of the HTS superconducting rectifier concepts published to date; their low magnet charging voltages, and the variable properties of their HTS-based switches. Our approach is to test a centre-tapped full-wave transformer–rectifier utilizing HTS secondary windings and switch-arrays of Si <sc xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mosfet</small>s mounted on a printed-circuit board (PCB). This approach has the advantage of greatly facilitating reproducible and reliable manufacture. The rectifier demonstrated magnet charging voltages exceeding a cycle-averaged 80 mV at 100 A and with typically more than 30% of the power supplied to the primary coils delivered to the magnet. We found it to be resilient to our preliminary thermal-cycling testing, with no degradation in performance observed over eight liquid-nitrogen to ambient (77–295 K) thermal cycles. We compare the impact of voltage- and current-controlled modes for the rectifier’s power supply. Our conclusion is that superconducting rectifiers using <sc xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mosfet</small> switch arrays placed on PCBs is a very promising approach for low-current HTS magnet power supplies.

papers.title_en: Compact High Turns Ratio Superconducting Transformer: Comparison Between Cu and REBCO Winding Materials
papers.abstract_en: Compact high turns ratio superconducting transformers are used to transfer power between low-current copper/ semiconductor-based circuits and high-current superconductor-based circuits. This type of transformer is a key component in devices, such as superconducting transformer rectifiers and superconducting current source inverters. Typically the copper winding and the superconducting winding are arranged with a turn ratio above 100:1, respectively, and are situated entirely within a cryogenic environment. The ohmic losses associated with the high count copper winding is problematic for most cryogenic applications and demands attention even when low currents on the order of 1–10 A are used. To address this problem, a transformer has been made using rare-earth barium copper oxide (REBCO) high-temperature superconductor (HTS) coated conductor for both the primary and secondary windings. The coupling coefficient and power consumption of this transformer were measured and compared to an equivalent transformer consisting of a copper primary winding and HTS secondary winding. The HTS primary was found to provide a significant reduction in transformer power consumption and a slight improvement to transformer coupling at frequencies below <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>8 Hz. An increased transformer core loss and winding AC loss began to negate these efficiency improvements above <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>8 Hz. In addition, cowinding the primary and secondary windings provided a higher coupling coefficient and lower power consumption for all winding combinations and frequencies tested. Finally, a short discussion on the implications of these findings respect to superconducting transformer rectifiers contextualizes the findings.

Mechanical Characteristics of Aluminium-Stabilized Stacked REBCO Tape Cable for the CEPC Detector Magnet
papers.abstract_en: This article investigates the mechanical characteristics and critical current performance of aluminum-stabilized stacked REBCO tape cable (ASTC) for the circular electron-positron collider detector magnet. In-plane bending, torsion, and uniaxial tension tests are carried out, combined by finite element analysis. The correlation between critical current and strain under different loading conditions is systematically analyzed, and key mechanical thresholds are determined. Results show that the minimum allowable in-plane bending diameter is 1200 mm. The critical twist pitch is 327 mm. The critical current degrades to 95% of the initial value when the tensile strain in the REBCO tape reaches 0.37%. This study provides essential experimental data and theoretical support for the structural design and engineering application of ASTC in high-field superconducting magnets.

papers.title_en: Designing Josephson Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifiers: EM-Circuit Cosimulation and Experimental Validation
papers.abstract_en: The development of large-scale superconducting quantum computers critically depends on the accurate readout of qubit states. To enable this, cryogenic parametric amplifiers have been proposed and developed, and have since found widespread use in small-signal detection applications. Among various amplifier architectures, Josephson traveling-wave parametric amplifiers (JTWPAs) are widely adopted due to their broad bandwidth, high saturation power, and compatibility with superconducting qubits. In this work, we present a design workflow of JTWPAs based on a cosimulation approach combining electromagnetic (EM) and circuit-level simulation. We apply this method to a uniform JTWPA, comparing our simulation results with experimental data. To mitigate the challenge of constructing lumped-element circuit models usually used in the conventional simulation method, we directly perform full EM analysis of the device to accurately determine its linear response. The extracted S-parameters are then fed into a nonlinear harmonic balance simulator with Josephson junctions modeled as circuit elements. By doing so, the linear and gain properties of the JTWPA are extracted. Different factors that impact device performance including gain compression, phase matching, and fabrication imperfections are further investigated and modeled. A good agreement between simulation and measurements is identified, establishing the effectiveness of our approach in designing quantum parametric amplifiers.

papers.title_en: Mathematics of effective q-plate in polarization optics
papers.abstract_en: The q-plate is a spatially inhomogeneous SU(2) birefringent optical element that has garnered significant interest due to its ability to mediate the spin-orbit interaction of light and facilitate the generation of structured light with singularities. The q-plate features a spatially varying fast axis orientation defined by three parameters: the topological charge q, retardance delta, and the offset angle $alpha_0$. While the parameter alpha_0 can be changed many times by rotation, any change in the charge and/or retardance entails the fabrication of a new plate. This limitation can be overcome through the concept of an effective waveplate, where multiple waveplates, homogeneous or inhomogeneous, are aligned coaxially so that, under specific constraints, the composite system emulates the behavior of a single effective waveplate. This work presents a comprehensive mathematical formalism for realizing an effective waveplate through a cascaded configuration of three q-plates, each chosen as either a quarter-wave q-plate, a half-wave q-plate, or a combination thereof. Some configurations offer tunability of the retardance over the full range from 0 to $2pi$, even though q-plates with fixed retardances of $pi/2$ and pi are used in sequence to form an effective q-plate. This feature enables holonomic polarization walk on the higher-order Poincare sphere. Such a capability holds significant potential for applications involving structured light associated with the higher-order Poincare sphere, particularly in controlled polarization transformations and polarization-topology engineering.

papers.title_en: Bayesian vs Deep learning: Parameter constraints for an anisotropic universe in f(Q) gravity
Quantum at the Edge: Scalable Standalone FPGA Emulator for QAOA-Based Weighted-MaxCut
papers.abstract_en: Quantum computing (QC) emulation is critical for exploring and advancing near-term quantum algorithms, given the ongoing scalability and reliability challenges of quantum hardware. While FPGA-based QC emulators have emerged as efficient alternatives to bridge the gap toward practical quantum computers, most existing solutions depend on high-performance systems, limiting their applicability in embedded and edge environments. In this work, we present a scalable, standalone FPGA-based emulator specialized for resource-constrained systems. Our design targets the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), particularly for the Weighted-MaxCut problem. By leveraging diagonal decomposition and a pipeline-centric hardware architecture, we reduce the computational complexity of QAOA from $\boldsymbol{O(N^{2})}$ to $\boldsymbol{O(N)}$, where $\boldsymbol{N}$ $\boldsymbol{=}$ $\boldsymbol{2^{n}}$ is the state dimension for $\boldsymbol{n}$ qubits. This reformulation and its architectural co-design significantly reduces hardware overhead, enabling larger qubit configurations on edge-level FPGAs. We encapsulate these optimizations into a hardware accelerator called the Quantum MaxCut Accelerator (QMA), which integrates seamlessly into a RISC-V platform, forming a self-contained emulator. Additionally, we introduce QC Emulator eXpress (QEX), a full-stack automation framework that streamlines QMA integration into configurable RISC-V platforms, significantly facilitating rapid and scalable emulator development and deployment. Through extensive prototyping of various QAOA emulators, our experiments confirm that the proposed QMA achieves energy reductions of up to $\textbf{907}\boldsymbol{\times}$ compared to the CPU-only software baseline under the same standalone FPGA/RISC-V setting and reliably supports up to 9 qubits on a mid-tier FPGA. These results demonstrate the energy efficiency and scalability of the proposed system as a self-contained FPGA/RISC-V platform for edge-local QAOA emulation, prototyping, and HW/SW co-design exploration under resource-constrained conditions.

papers.title_en: Theory of double flat-top solitons in coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations
papers.abstract_en: Solitons are fundamental entities in nonlinear wave equations across diverse branches of physics. In systems with competing nonlinearities, a hallmark transition occurs from traditional bell-shaped profiles to flat-top configurations as the norm increases. In this work, we analyze double flat-top solitons in systems of two coupled generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equations. We develop a theoretical and variational framework that provides both physical insight and a computationally efficient description of these eigenstates. In the large-norm regime, and for a broad class of nonlinear potentials supporting flat-top states, we derive explicit analytical expressions for the plateau densities and chemical potentials, together with variational estimates for the interfacial properties characterizing the solutions. These quantities are controlled by algebraic conditions that generalize the Maxwell coexistence condition to coupled wave functions. We show that two-component flat-top solitons may form core–shell configurations, in which a two-component core is surrounded by a shell of the dominant species, as well as no-shell configurations, where both species occupy the same spatial domain. Using the cubic-quintic nonlinearity as a prototypical model, we compare these analytical predictions with direct numerical computations of the stationary states and find excellent agreement in the flat-top regime. The resulting picture admits a natural interpretation in terms of phase coexistence in an effective binary fluid, with kink-like interfaces carrying an excess grand potential that plays the role of a surface tension. This formalism is applicable to diverse physical platforms, including nonlinear optics, multicomponent Bose–Einstein condensates, and Q-ball configurations in relativistic field theories.

papers.title_en: Quantum Key Distribution Based Physical Layer Security Applied in Complex Modulation Formats for Optical Fiber Links
papers.abstract_en: A Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) based Physical Layer Security (PLS) scheme (QKD-PLS) for optical fiber links is proposed and evaluated. In detail, a novel amplitude and phase scrambling technique for exploiting and seamlessly integrating high key rate QKD for the encryption of the modulation parameters of conventional complex modulation schemes like M-ary Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (M-QAM) and Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) is described. Scrambling is applied to both preamble (pilot signals) and payload segments of the transmission frame, to prevent the eavesdroppers from performing vital receiver functionalities such as frame synchronization and channel estimation. Additionally, a practical Key Management System (KMS) taking care of all key synchronization processes is developed and introduced. Moreover, another advantage of QKD exploitation to the proposed solution comes from the application of high entropy kbps-rate QKD keys feeding pseudo-random number generators, to modify the broadband modulation symbols in one-time pad, therefore significantly improving data protection. Experimental evaluation via a transmission scenario in fiber links is also presented, depicting the efficacy of the QKD-PLS.

papers.title_en: Holography and the Quantum Nature of Black Holes
papers.abstract_en: Black holes pose a lot of unsolved problems surrounding their fundamental properties. One of those puzzles is the black hole entropy problem. It has been known for a long time that black holes behave as thermodynamic systems and possess an entropy, but the question remains which microstates are responsible for this entropy. A theory of quantum gravity is needed to tackle this problem, currently the most viable example of which is string theory. The work of Strominger and Vafa, where they studied a class of asymptotically flat black holes, proves that string theory is indeed rich enough to account for the microstates responsible for the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy. Recently, the focus has shifted to asymptotically AdS black holes after the discovery of the AdS/CFT correspondence.Holographic dualities, the first example of which was discovered by Maldacena, have proven to be highly successful in providing a microstate counting for the entropy of black holes. The black hole is constructed on the gravity side of the correspondence, and the dual field theory counts its states. In this thesis we study black holes in AdS5 and their dual 4d N=1 SCFTs. The general procedure can be summarized as follows. On the field theory side, supersymmetric states are counted using the superconformal index. From the index we can obtain the entropy via a Legendre transform. By requiring that the entropy is real, we obtain a prediction for the existence of a dual black hole with that same entropy. In the dual supergravity theory we look for such solutions and compute the Euclidean on-shell action to match to the index, and the horizon area to match to the CFT entropy.This procedure was successfully applied to the minimal sector of any AdS5/CFT4 duality by Cabo-Bizet, Cassani, Martelli and Murthy, to leading order in the large N expansion. Here we aim to move beyond these results by adding flavour symmetries to the problem and by going beyond leading order at large N. On the field theory side of the duality, we study the index and entropy of flavoured SCFTs. We observe that for some theories, the simple procedure for taking the Legendre transform in the literature can no longer be applied. In all previously known examples, the index satisfies a cubic identity which leads to a simple way of deriving the entropy. We show that this identity no longer holds for certain theories but can be replaced by a sixth order identity, resulting in a different, more complicated expression for the entropy. These results suggest the existence of a new class of dual black hole solutions to match this entropy with their horizon area.We then proceed to finding these new solutions. This is a highly nontrivial problem because the dual supergravity theories contain hypermultiplet scalars. We specifically choose to work in the duality derived from M5-branes wrapping around a Riemann surface, between a family of non-Lagrangian class S SCFTs and a set of N=2 supergravities with two vector multiplets and one hypermultiplet, both parametrized by a rational number z. For z=±1, the cubic identity is satisfied and the entropy takes the familiar, simple form. Here we can easily identify the dual black holes through a relation to the five-dimensional STU model. For other values of z, we need the sixth order identity and we must include the hypermultiplet scalars in the black hole solution. To simplify the problem, we look for the near-horizon extremal geometry and restrict to two equal angular momenta. We start from the known solution for z=1 and perform an expansion around this point. We find an analytical solution to first order in the expansion. Since we only solve in the near-horizon region, we lose access to the on-shell action and chemical potentials but can still compute the charges and the entropy. The entropy through the area law matches precisely with the field theory prediction. We therefore prove that these partial solutions are the first step towards identifying the new class of black hole solutions with non-zero hypermultiplet scalars.In the final part of this thesis we move beyond the leading order at large N and add higher-derivative corrections. We focus on the universal case where only the R-symmetry is turned on. In this case, the higher-derivative action including four derivatives can be fully determined up to two constants, which can be related to the conformal anomalies of the dual field theory using the holographic map. We then set out to confirm the first subleading corrections to the index and entropy from the gravity side of the duality. We argue that the corrections to the black hole solution are not needed for the Euclidean on-shell action. It suffices to substitute the leading order solution in the corrected action. We perform this calculation carefully and obtain a precise match with the superconformal index. For the entropy, the corrections to the solution are needed. Here we opt to compute the entropy from the quantum statistical relation and the first law. Finally, we comment on higher-derivative corrections to flavoured theories.

papers.title_en: Floquet quantum gates with ion-enhanced Rydberg blockade
papers.abstract_en: Direct Rydberg-Rydberg interactions decay rapidly with distance, limiting blockade-based gates between spatially separated neutral-atom qubits. We study a hybrid architecture in which a trapped ion mediates an additional effective interaction between two Rydberg atoms in optical tweezers. Following the ion-mediated mechanism [S. Mudli, S. Mal. S. S. Rej, A. Dey, and B. Deb, Phys. Rev. A 110, 062618 (2024)], we identify the total blockade interaction that enters the conditional gate dynamics and state the perturbative conditions under which the second-order Magnus description applies. We then use Floquet-modulated ground-Rydberg drives to construct cnot and controlled-<math><mi>T</mi></math> gates for a prescribed strong-blockade ratio. Numerical simulations show fidelities above 0.998 in the coherent model and reduced sensitivity to the sampled Rabi-frequency and detuning errors. Atomic spontaneous emission lowers the fidelity, with the shorter controlled-<math><mi>T</mi></math> sequence being less affected than the cnot sequence. We distinguish these effective-blockade simulations from a complete experimental error budget: ion heating, excess micromotion, trap-frequency noise, and residual atom-motion entanglement are not included numerically and must be controlled in an implementation. The results establish a concrete connection between ion-mediated blockade enhancement and Floquet-robust conditional control while defining the regime and limitations of the effective model.

papers.title_en: Factorization in quasifree breakup reactions with two bodies left behind
papers.abstract_en: We consider scenarios in which a shallow bound state undergoes breakup by a probe whose energy is high compared to the binding energy. The first two scenarios, which serve as warm-up exercises, involve a single heavy particle bound to a light particle, analogous to a core nucleus bound to a neutron. We show that in quasifree kinematics, the leading effect comes from the heavy particle being knocked out by the probe, with corrections suppressed by inverse powers of the probe momentum. This formally justifies extracting neutron form factors from high-energy deuteron breakup in quasifree kinematics. In scenario 1, the probe is a local current; in scenario 2, it is hadron scattering. In scenarios 3 and 4 we consider, respectively, a local current and hadron scattering, but now on a three-body bound state of a heavy particle and two light particles. Hard knockout of the heavy particle leaves two low-energy particles behind, which can interact with one another. In all four scenarios, we prove that the amplitude is dominated by the nearby on-shell pole of the heavy-particle propagator and derive a closed-form expression for this contribution. When two bodies are left behind, the leading amplitude is the product of the scattering of the two light particles, a dynamical function depending on the probe, and a real function related to the bound-state wave function. Thus, quasifree removal of a core nucleus from a system with halo neutrons provides access to on-shell data on multineutron interactions. The resulting amplitudes are relativistic and satisfy unitarity for the remnant subsystem exactly. We also provide complementary nonrelativistic derivations. While the derivations are for spinless particles, the generalization to spin is straightforward, since the results depend only on quasifree knockout kinematics; we make no assumptions about the interparticle dynamics.

papers.title_en: Non-Hermitian Michelson interferometer for exceptional-point-enhanced sensing
papers.abstract_en: The Michelson interferometer underpins modern optical metrology, enabling precise measurements of displacement and gravitational waves. However, the sensitivity of the conventional Hermitian Michelson interferometer is inherently limited by its linear response to a perturbation. Here, we propose a non-Hermitian Michelson interferometer by introducing a coupling between two arms with reservoir engineering, forming a configuration of light cross. The eigenfrequency splitting as a spectral response displays a square-root dependence on a perturbation. Remarkably, the quantum Fisher information of our non-Hermitian Michelson interferometer can exceed that of its Hermitian counterpart by more than three orders when Brownian noise is included, implying a great enhancement in sensitivity. This work provides a framework for non-Hermitian interferometric sensing with unprecedented sensitivity.

papers.title_en: Cosmological Constraints and Bayesian Evidence for Coupled $\phi$CDM with DESI DR2 Observations
papers.abstract_en:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We investigate a coupled $\phi$CDM cosmological model in which energy exchange between dark energy and dark matter is governed by the derivative interaction term $Q = 3\alpha \dot{\rho}_m$. We constrain the model using baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from DESI Data Release~2, combined with compressed CMB likelihoods and  Type~Ia supernova datasets, including Pantheon$^{+}$, DES-Dovekie, and Union3. Parameter estimation is performed via Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods, and Bayesian evidence is used for model comparison with $\Lambda$CDM. We find that the interaction parameter $\alpha$ is tightly constrained at the $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4})$ level and remains consistent with zero within $1\sigma$ across all dataset combinations, indicating no statistically significant evidence for dark sector interaction. The dark energy equation-of-state parameter remains close to $w_{\phi}=-1$, with only mild and statistically insignificant deviations toward a quintessence-like regime. While the inferred Hubble parameter shows a slight shift to higher values relative to $\Lambda$CDM, it remains insufficient to resolve the $H_0$ tension. The matter density parameter is consistent between both models within uncertainties. Bayesian model comparison consistently favors the $\Lambda$CDM model, with evidence ranging from moderate to strong depending on the dataset combination. Overall, the \textcolor{red}{coupled} $\phi$CDM model does not provide a significant improvement over the standard cosmological scenario in light of current observations.</jats:p>

papers.title_en: Models Developed to Describe FRIIb and FRIIa Radio Sources
papers.abstract_en:
Several models developed to describe the properties of FRIIa and FRIIb radio
sources are compared and contrasted here. The fundamental picture of a classical double (edge-brightened, FRII) radio source powered by highly collimated outflows from a central compact object is common to most models. However, models do diﬀer substantially, and some of the key diﬀerences are discussed here. Models must be tested and constrained by comparisons with radio data. The extensive, detailed, radio data that can be used to constrain the physical properties of FRII sources will be described. The radio bridge properties of FRII sources indicates they should be divided into two categories: FRIIa and FRIIb sources. Low-power FRIIa sources are typically found at low-redshift and have distorted radio bridge structure. High-power FRIIb sources are typically found at high-redshift and have fairly regular, “cigar-like” bridge shapes. It is anticipated that two model formalisms may be needed to describe
FRIIb and FRIIa sources. Unlike FRIIa sources, FRIIb sources are found to inhabit
gaseous environments similar to those found in low-redshift clusters of galaxies, though the sources have redshifts between zero and two. Thus, FRIIb sources most likely lie in clusters of galaxies. The importance of X-ray measurements to determine the density and temperature of the gas in the vicinity of FRIIb sources is stressed.

papers.title_en: <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> spectroscopy using <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>13</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>(<math><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></math>) resonant elastic scattering
papers.abstract_en: The detailed excitation functions for <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>13</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> elastic scattering and the additional thick target inverse kinematics measurements were analyzed using the <math><mi>R</mi></math> matrix approach. The analysis covered the excitation region in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math> from 8.6 up to 11.2 MeV. Information on single particle widths of the levels in the <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nucleus and shell model calculations are in good agreement. A comparative analysis of the <math><mi>α</mi></math>-cluster structures of <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nuclei indicates their common underlying nature. However, the structure in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math> is more complex. In particular, each <math><mi>α</mi></math>-cluster level with spin <math><mi>J</mi></math> in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts></math> corresponds to several levels with spins <math><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. Unexpectedly, the reduced-width-weighted centroids of the higher-spin members of these doublets always lie at lower excitation energies in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math>.

papers.title_en: Investigating two-body cluster structures of <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>10</mn></mmultiscripts></math>
papers.abstract_en: Two-body breakup mechanisms of the weakly bound nucleus <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>10</mn></mmultiscripts></math> were investigated through an exclusive coincidence measurement in the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>10</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Au</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>197</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> system at a beam energy of 57 MeV. Coincident detection of two outgoing charged particles by an array of Si strip detector telescopes shows that the dominant two-body projectile breakup channels are <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Li</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>6</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>9</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>. Projectile excitation energies, reconstructed from the kinetic energies of the fragments, are found to reproduce the energies of specific excited states of <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>10</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and thereby confirm the coexistence of both <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Li</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>6</mn></mmultiscripts><mtext>-</mtext><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>9</mn></mmultiscripts><mtext>-</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> two-body cluster configurations for <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>10</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. Continuum discretized coupled channels (CDCC) calculations, considering each of the above two cluster configurations separately, were able to explain the experimental cross sections for both breakup as well as elastic scattering simultaneously.

papers.title_en: Experimental study of the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>6</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>5</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction at 52 MeV: Probing the single-neutron wave function of the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>6</mn></mmultiscripts></math> ground state
papers.abstract_en: New experimental data for the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>6</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>5</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> one-neutron pickup reaction at 52 MeV were measured in inverse kinematics at the ACCULINNA-2 isotope in-flight separator at the Flerov Laboratory of Nuclear Reactions, Joint Institute for Nuclear Research, Dubna. The data were analyzed using two standard direct reaction models, the distorted wave Born approximation (DWBA) and coupled reaction channels. Single neutron wave functions for the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>6</mn></mmultiscripts></math> ground state obtained using three different nuclear structure methods, including the new cluster channel orthogonal function method, were tested and the dependence of the results of the reaction calculations on the properties of these wave functions was observed. The data were well reproduced by a DWBA calculation with the wave function obtained using the ab initio variational Monte Carlo method with no adjustable parameters.

papers.title_en: Possible coexistence of pseudospin partner bands and wobbling excitation in triaxial nuclei
papers.abstract_en: It has been conventionally assumed that triaxial deformation breaks the degeneracy of pseudospin doublets, leading to less discussion of pseudospin partner bands in triaxial nuclei. However, by considering the pairing correlations, the quasiparticle states of pseudospin doublets are found to remain nearly degenerate at appropriate Fermi energies in triaxial systems. In this work, we systematically investigate the pseudospin partner bands based on the <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> configuration in triaxial nuclei using the particle rotor model. For the first time, we propose the possible coexistence of pseudospin partner bands and wobbling excitation. Further analysis of angular momentum geometry and wave function components supports the identification of one structure as a pseudospin partner band and the other as a wobbling band. This study reveals a novel coexistence mode between pseudospin partner bands and wobbling excitation, illustrating the diversity of rotational excitations in atomic nuclei.

papers.title_en: Structure and decay of <math><mi>α</mi></math>-condensate candidates from cluster effective field theory interactions
papers.abstract_en: Dilute gas-like configurations of <math><mi>α</mi></math> particles, often termed <math><mi>α</mi></math> condensates, have been proposed to exist in certain excited states of <math><mi>α</mi></math>-conjugate nuclei. This work investigates the structural and decay properties of <math><mi>α</mi></math>-condensate candidates within a few-body framework using leading-order cluster effective field theory interactions. To isolate dilute <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> configurations, a constrained model space strategy is implemented inspired by Yamada and Schuck [Phys. Rev. C 69, 024309 (2004)], which constructs a description specifically for suprathreshold states. By explicitly decoupling the nonuniversal, compact configurations lying below the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> threshold, this framework describes <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> condensates as quasibound states localized within the Coulomb barrier. The stochastic variational method is used to perform theoretical calculations for the proposed <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> condensates ranging from <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>8</mn></mmultiscripts></math> to <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ne</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>20</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. The results not only map the formation of these novel cluster states in heavier <math><mi>α</mi></math>-conjugate nuclei but also offer critical insights into the applicability of few-body universality to charged particles.

papers.title_en: Critical response and enhanced parameter sensitivity in gapless fermionic systems
papers.abstract_en: Quantum Fisher information (QFI) quantifies the infinitesimal distance between two quantum states and characterizes the ultimate precision limit for the estimation of a parameter. While critical enhancement of QFI is well understood in gapped systems, its behavior in gapless topological phases remains less explored. In this work, we establish a general scaling criterion governing the emergence of singular many-body QFI in gapless fermionic systems. We show that, although single-particle QFI generically diverges near band-closing points when a control parameter shifts the position of the node, whether this divergence survives at the many-body level is determined by the codimension of the gapless manifold. Specifically, we demonstrate that in three-dimensional systems, the many-body QFI density diverges only when the codimension is less than or equal to two. This result leads to a sharp metrological distinction between Weyl semimetals and nodal-line semimetals. Furthermore, we construct explicit measurement protocols that saturate the quantum Cramér-Rao bound, showing that the predicted enhancement is, in principle, accessible via mode-resolved measurements. These results establish a direct connection among band topology, quantum geometry, and quantum metrology.

papers.title_en: Imaginarity-assisted minimum error discrimination
papers.abstract_en: Minimum error discrimination is a general approach for quantum-state discrimination. This work establishes a connection between quantum imaginarity and minimum error discrimination, investigating the conditions under which auxiliary quantum states can enhance the maximum average success probability (MASP) with real positive-operator-valued measures (POVMs) or even achieve the MASP attainable with general POVMs. We prove that an auxiliary quantum state is nonreal if and only if it can enhance the MASP attainable with real POVMs in the composite system for at least one discrimination task. In particular, for pure states, only auxiliary maximally imaginary states can achieve the unrestricted MASP for all discrimination tasks. For a fixed ensemble, the assisted advantage is a convex, strongly monotonic imaginarity quantifier, but it need not be faithful. We characterize the ensembles for which it is faithful through a one-parameter family of discrimination problems and derive a spectral criterion for binary ensembles. These results identify when assisted discrimination efficiency defines a faithful imaginarity measure and clarify the operational role of imaginarity under real measurement constraints.

papers.title_en: Maximum confidence channel discrimination: Probe design, entanglement assistance, and sequential measurement
papers.abstract_en: In this work, we study maximum confidence measurement for quantum channel discrimination and develop optimization-based algorithms for designing both the probe state and measurement operators. We show that entanglement-assisted strategies with pure probe states and bounded reference dimensions suffice to achieve optimal performance. We characterize the optimal probe as a weakly Pareto optimal point of the achievable confidence region, and illustrate the framework on complementary dephasing qubit channels for which this region, the minimax probe, and the sequential design are obtained in closed form. Finally, we extend the framework to sequential maximum confidence measurements, where multiple observers perform measurements sequentially while maintaining the same confidence guarantees.

papers.title_en: Transport simulations with a constrained momentum-dependent chiral mean-field equation of state at various isospin fractions
papers.abstract_en: We present a comparison of the ultrarelativistic quantum molecular dynamics model using a chiral mean field (CMF) equation of state with flow and pion production data in heavy ion collisions at low beam energies <math><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>lab</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>2.0</mn><mspace width="0.16em"/><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> GeV and varying isospin fraction. The CMF model parameters are constrained by known properties of the high density equation of state of quantum chromodynamics at varying isospin fractions. This allows us to calculate the equation of state as well as nuclear interactions for different physical systems like neutron stars and heavy ion collisions in a consistent way. It is found that heavy ion reactions at the upcoming FAIR facility will only have marginal sensitivity on the isospin dependence of the high-density equation of state. At lower beam energies, comparing to FOPI, HADES, and <math><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>π</mi><mtext>RIT</mtext></mrow></math> data, the sensitivity is higher but the observed deviations and systematic uncertainties of the existing data are larger than the sensitivity to the symmetry energy.

papers.title_en: Nearly Optimal Quantum Sample Complexity of Learning Fourier-Sparse Boolean Functions
papers.abstract_en: We study the number of uniform quantum examples needed to exactly learn a Boolean function with at most $k$ nonzero Fourier coefficients. We give a learner with near-optimal $\widetilde{O}(k)$ sample complexity independent of the input length $n$. The learner uses only separate measurements of individual examples. This improves the previous $O(k^{3/2}\log^2 k)$ upper bound (Arunachalam, Chakraborty, Lee, Paraashar, and de Wolf, 2021). The main ingredient is a candidate set formed by symmetric differences of subsets from independent groups of Fourier samples. A multilinear majority polynomial combines unbiased random approximations into an accurate witness whose Fourier support lies in this set. Granularity then forces the set to contain the entire Fourier support, including subsets never directly sampled. For comparison, we derive the tight classical sample complexity $Θ(nk)$ by combining known sparse-recovery and lower-bound results.

papers.title_en: QEDIA: Quantum Program Verification in Lean
papers.abstract_en: Practical quantum programs interleave quantum and classical computation: classical data shape the quantum operations that are performed, and measurement outcomes shape the classical computation that follows. Formal verification of such programs in a proof assistant requires mechanizing a program logic that handles this interplay consistently at every level, from the mathematics of quantum mechanics, through program syntax and semantics, to specifications and proof rules. Such mechanizations, along with the program proofs built on them, typically require substantial manual effort. We present QEDIA, a framework for verifying quantum programs with classical variables in Lean 4. At its foundation is an open library that formalizes the quantum Hoare logic QHL+ across all these levels and proves the logic sound for both partial and total correctness. We construct the library and the program proofs, under human supervision, using an LLM-based prover agent, whose general-purpose core we extend for quantum program verification. We illustrate QEDIA with verified programs including the quantum Fourier transform, phase estimation, repeat-until-success circuits, and Hamiltonian simulation.

papers.title_en: A Tutorial on Quantum Amplitude Embedding with Data Re-Uploading
papers.abstract_en: Amplitude embedding lets a variational quantum model read many classical features with few qubits, but the model output is then only a quadratic form in the normalized input. Data re-uploading, which encodes the input repeatedly between trainable blocks, can be used to enrich such a model. Because every additional upload of an amplitude embedding repeats a costly state preparation, the gain that an upload buys has to be known before the gates are spent. This tutorial thus addresses the problem of explaining what data re-uploading adds to an amplitude-embedded model and how large the gain is. We express sequential re-uploading and parallel re-uploading with two copies in one notation and show that each upload raises the reachable polynomial order by two. Under one trainable circuit family and one budget of trainable parameters, simulation results show that re-uploading raises the test coefficient of determination from 0.689 to between 0.883 and 0.975 on targets of order four and from 0.337 to between 0.642 and 0.783 on targets of order six, on all ten seeds. On a quadratic target and on handwritten digits, one upload remains the best choice, and every additional upload lowers the gate error that the classifier tolerates. These results help designers match the number of uploads to the polynomial order of the task at hand.

papers.title_en: Distance Prediction for Quantum Codes
papers.abstract_en: The distance of a quantum code is a fundamental metric that dictates its error-correction capability. While quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) families such as Bivariate Bicycle (BB) codes offer a promising pathway to low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computing, computing their distance is challenging. Current exact solvers and even search heuristics that provide a distance upper bound suffer from severe computational bottlenecks, restricting the discovery of optimal codes. In this paper, we construct a dataset of BB codes with corresponding distance upper bounds obtained through high-budget heuristic searches. We introduce BB-Net, an attention-based neural network architecture for predicting the distance of BB codes. It achieves 96.39% accuracy on the reference distances in the test set, compared with 94.86% for state-of-the-art heuristics with a budget of up to $10^{4}$ times more computational runtime. On a subset with certified exact distances, BB-Net achieves 98.94%. By relieving the distance-calculation bottleneck, BB-Net enables faster screening of large code spaces, particularly in ML-driven search pipelines, and thereby can accelerate the discovery of novel quantum error-correcting codes, an important capability for advancing scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing. Our code is publicly available: https://github.com/NadavSc/BBNet

papers.title_en: Representation Geometry and Inductive Biases in Quantum Classifiers across Classical Visual Benchmarks
papers.abstract_en: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has a theoretical advantage over classical algorithms for specific synthetic data that is computationally hard. However, it remains unclear whether such theoretical advantages play a meaningful role for realistic classical data, such as natural images. Quantum structural properties induced by unitary operations or entanglement introduce inductive biases that differ from those of classical models, potentially leading to distinct learning behavior on real-world data. In a fully quantum learning pipeline, classical real-world data are first encoded into quantum states via a quantum feature mapping, analogous to a classical feature extractor, and a quantum classifier then classifies the resulting states. Quantum feature mappings generate representations that are difficult to realize classically, while also inducing representation-level biases that do not necessarily match the structure of realistic data. To enable a fair comparison at the classifier level, we focus on the classifier and use classical feature extractors that already provide powerful representations for natural images. By controlling the data scale and supervision strength, we analyze how the unitary structure of quantum classifiers affects generalization, and show that their effectiveness depends strongly on the geometry of the input representations. These results indicate that quantum classifiers benefit from classical features that are aligned with quantum feature spaces. Our analysis shows that kernel alignment identifies representations compatible with quantum feature spaces, providing insights into translating classical models into quantum algorithms.

papers.title_en: PADO-Pauli: A GPU-Accelerated Implementation of Pauli Propagation
papers.abstract_en: Variational quantum algorithms utilize parameterized circuits many times during training, at new parameter values, over batches of data, and with gradients. Pauli propagation approximates the expectation values of such circuits classically by evolving the observable in the Heisenberg picture as a truncated sum of Pauli strings. We present PADO-Pauli, a GPU engine for Pauli propagation that compiles a circuit and its observables once into sparse matrices in which each rotation angle contributes only a cosine and a sine factor, so every later evaluation reuses the compiled program. It evaluates batches of parameters and data inputs embedded as rotation angles. By default its gradients come from a vector-Jacobian product registered with PyTorch's automatic differentiation, so they flow through the angles to any classical layer that produces them. PADO-Pauli also provides truncation by Pauli weight and coefficient size, and noise channels. Zero-filtering removes terms that do not contribute to an expectation value in the all-zero reference state and makes the batched forward pass about 1.5 times faster. Compared to cuPauliProp on an NVIDIA A100, PADO-Pauli evaluates up to 10 times faster on 4 to 12 qubits and uses up to 3.1 times less memory on 16 qubits. We check its accuracy against exact statevector simulation up to 28 qubits. These features make PADO-Pauli a practical toolkit for training variational quantum algorithms, including quantum machine learning models.

papers.title_en: Lifting: Quantum State Discrimination Framework for Mid-Circuit Measurements
papers.abstract_en: Quantum computing promises new capabilities beyond classical computation. Mid-circuit measurements (MCMs) enable error correction and outcome-dependent control, but their reliability is limited by noise on superconducting hardware. These operations depend on accurate quantum state discrimination (QSD), which assigns measured signals to state labels. Neural network-based (NN-based) QSD improves this assignment, yet its error remains bounded below by the Bayes risk of the available readout distributions. A complementary challenge is state deterioration as successive measurements accumulate and circuit execution advances, making static calibration less representative of the workload. We present Lifting, a QSD framework that addresses both challenges through repetition encoding, neural decoding, and in situ calibration. Encoding supplies joint in-phase and quadrature (I-Q) readout signals from the target and auxiliary qubits, while contextual calibration trains the decoder for the conditions encountered during execution. Our theoretical analysis shows that retaining additional channels from a fixed joint distribution cannot increase Bayes risk and establishes sufficient conditions for contraction of an overlap-based upper bound. Experiments across three IBM processors evaluate the framework on repeated stabilizer measurement, parity-check, and teleportation workloads.

papers.title_en: Steering the Fidelity in State Preparation on Noisy Bosonic Systems with Risk-Seeking Optimization
papers.abstract_en: In order to execute quantum algorithms on bosonic quantum computers, it is necessary to encode their inputs into a desired target quantum state, with a process called state preparation. In real settings, state preparation methods operate in stochastic scenarios, where the prepared state is represented as a mixed state, that is a probabilistic ensemble of pure states. Therefore, existing state preparation methods optimize a variational ansatz by averaging over all possible sequences of photon loss events contained in the prepared ensemble, yielding an output state which approximates the desired target with a certain average fidelity. Such an approach, however, does not take into account directly the distribution of fidelities across states in the ensemble. In this work, we aim to maximize the fidelity of only a subset of pure states sampled from the prepared ensemble, at the cost of reducing the average fidelity overall. This trade-off is relevant when the goal is to obtain high-fidelity states with a certain probability, rather than maximizing the average fidelity of the prepared ensemble. We borrow and adapt objective functions from risk-sensitive optimization, a framework that optimizes specific characteristics of a distribution rather than only its expectation, and that has been successfully applied in Reinforcement Learning. In the considered experimental settings, our results show that the infidelities of some pure states in the prepared ensemble can be reduced by up to four orders of magnitude when using risk-seeking objectives, compared to those achieved using the standard optimization of the average fidelity. Furthermore, we show that it is possible to control the trade-off between the probability of obtaining high-fidelity states and the lowest infidelity threshold reached, providing the flexibility to select the operating point that best suits a certain application.

papers.title_en: Dynamical BEC formation and vanishing entropy for trapped bosons in non-relativistic QED via nonlinear resonance cascades
papers.abstract_en:
The dynamical formation of a complete Bose-Einstein condensate and the asymptotic purification of trapped bosons coupled to a quantized radiation field are rigorously established. By tracking the macroscopic one-particle density matrix $κ_T$ through a nonlinear resonance cascade, it is demonstrated that radiative relaxation irreversibly depletes all excited trap modes, even when the initial macroscopic state $κ_0$ is genuinely mixed. Here $κ_T$ is an average, with respect to a de Finetti measure $μ_0$, over mean-field particle-field orbits, so that the mixedness of $κ_0$ reflects a statistical ensemble of orbits. Under the assumptions of a non-vanishing initial ground state component and strictly positive downward Fermi-Golden-Rule rates, strong trace-norm convergence to a pure condensate is proven, 
$$ \lim_{T\to\infty} \| κ_T-|χ_0\rangle\langleχ_0| \|_{\mathfrak{S}_1(\mathfrak{h})} = 0 \, . $$
 Furthermore, the von Neumann entropy of the macroscopic one-particle density matrix is shown to vanish asymptotically, 
$$ \lim_{T\to\infty}S[κ_T]=0 \, , $$
 without any claim of monotonicity in $T$. Thus, any initially mixed, positive-entropy state ($0<S[κ_0]<\infty$) is purified to the ground state $|χ_0\rangle\langleχ_0|$. For the proof, we derive the Hartree hierarchy of the coupled system of bosons and photons from the finite-$N$ BBGKY hierarchy of the microscopic quantum many-body system, establishing trace-norm convergence in the mean-field limit as $N\to\infty$. The limits are taken successively; first $N\to\infty$, then the weak-coupling limit, and finally $T\to\infty$. Although the global particle-field evolution remains unitary, the macroscopic one-particle state converges to a pure state as energy and correlations are continuously radiated into the dispersive field.

papers.title_en: On quasi-lisse affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories
papers.abstract_en: We study certain simple affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is a non-simply-laced simple Lie algebra and $h$ is its Coxeter number. For $L_{-3}(F_4)$, we determine the maximal ideal of $V^{-3}(F_4)$, Zhu's algebra, and the associated variety. We also classify the irreducible highest-weight $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules and determine the characters of its irreducible ordinary modules. The associated variety is $\overline{\mathbb{O}}_{\widetilde A_1}$, and the level $-3$ is totally collapsing for the orbit $\mathbb{O}_{\widetilde A_1}$. The Poisson coinvariants of the $C_2$-algebra of $L_{-3}(F_4)$ are isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}[\ell]/(\ell^5)$, where $\ell$ is induced by the conformal vector. Consequently, the characters of ordinary $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules satisfy a fifth-order modular linear differential equation. We also give modular linear differential equations of orders five and eleven satisfied by the characters of ordinary modules for $L_{-2}(B_3)$ and $L_{-2}(G_2)$ respectively.

papers.title_en: Classical and quantum scattering of massive Klein--Gordon fields in asymptotically flat spacetimes
papers.abstract_en: We use microlocal tools to define distinguished incoming and outgoing vacuum states of the quantum theory of massive Klein--Gordon fields in non-trapping asymptotically flat spacetimes, including radiative perturbations of Minkowski space. The asymptotic vacuum states satisfy the Hadamard condition, and the incoming and outgoing particle representations are unitarily equivalent, or in other words the quantum S-matrix is well-defined. These results are based on a description of scattering of classical fields which keeps track of the asymptotic distinction between positive- and negative-frequency solutions of the Klein--Gordon equation. Our emphasis is on developing the theory without recourse to explicit asymptotics for classical waves.

papers.title_en: Beyond the circle: current algebras, geometry and higher gauge structures
papers.abstract_en: Replacing the circle by a manifold leads to current Lie algebras and their central and derivation extensions. We separate the coefficient algebra, harmonic analysis and geometric data. Differentials modulo exact forms describe central extensions; divergence-free vector fields give explicit cocycles, whose compatible derivations satisfy a stabilizer equation. Compact examples include the three-sphere and its current--Virasoro extension. We also explain the analytic qualifications for SL(2,R) and its symmetric space and the role of transported multiplication in soft geometries. The recent harmonic constructions of Campoamor-Stursberg, Marrani and Rausch de Traubenberg are compared with the cohomological work of Coquereaux, Frappat, Ragoucy and Sorba and Castellani's loop geometry and infinite-dimensional free differential algebras. A coefficient-algebra construction connects currents to higher brackets and clarifies the additional requirements of a dynamical theory. For Lie algebras of order F, central extensions obey coupled binary and symmetric F-ary conditions, with explicit examples and obstructions.

papers.title_en: Dynamics of low energy wave packets in the one-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet
papers.abstract_en: Spin wave theory plays a central role in the analysis of low-energy properties of the quantum ferromagnetic Heisenberg model. In this work, we present a first step towards a rigorous justification of this approximation in the context of quantum dynamics in one dimension. According to spin wave theory, the evolution of a spin wave state should be well approximated by its free evolution with the appropriate energy of free quasiparticles called magnons. Our main result establishes this idea rigorously for a class of spin wave packets. We focus on spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ systems, and consider wave packets composed of two magnons. We argue our result is optimal with respect to the timescales.

papers.title_en: How many switches does two-Hamiltonian universality require?
papers.abstract_en: Any pair of sufficiently generic Hamiltonians on $\mathbb{C}^d$ generates the full unitary group, i.e., any $W\in U(d)$ can be synthesized to arbitrary precision by alternating between the two evolutions for suitably chosen durations. For any given pair of Hamiltonians, the minimal number of switches required to cover the entire group is at least $d$ and unbounded in general. Despite this, we show that it scales linearly in $d$ in expectation. Assuming that the two spectra are sufficiently generic, we derive constructive upper bounds on the minimal switching number as a function of the change-of-basis matrix between the two eigenbases. In particular, if this matrix has a column whose entries all have equal moduli, as for a complex Hadamard matrix, then $9d$ switches suffice to reach every unitary. To obtain these results, we construct a short exact representation of any unitary as a product of unitaries that are alternately diagonal in two given bases. All bounds are extended to non-generic spectra and bounded evolution times.

papers.title_en: Supersymmetric Observables from Surface Defect Anomalies in 4d and 6d SCFTs
papers.abstract_en: We study the contributions of half-BPS surface defects to supersymmetric Casimir energy and the universal logarithmic term of supersymmetric Rényi entropy in four- and six-dimensional SCFTs. Using equivariant integration of defect anomaly polynomials and its extension to supersymmetric Rényi backgrounds, we obtain closed expressions for these observables in terms of defect 't Hooft anomalies. For Gukov--Witten defects preserving transverse rotations in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = 4$ super Yang--Mills theories, both observables depend on a single R-symmetry anomaly. For $\mathcal{N} = (0, 4)$ defects in six-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = (1, 0)$ theories, additional terms arise from the gravitational anomaly. We provide complementary checks using chiral algebras, five-dimensional localization, and holographic probe branes at large $N$, while localized chiral fermions reproduce the gravitational-anomaly contributions. The framework also recovers Wilson-surface results in six-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = (2, 0)$ theories.

papers.title_en: Stable manifolds of heteroclinic chains in Hořava-Lifshitz cosmology
papers.abstract_en: We consider vacuum spatially homogeneous models in Hořava-Lifshitz gravity, which are expected to describe generic singularities for these modified gravity theories. These models perturb the well-known Bianchi models in general relativity (GR) by a parameter $v\in (0,1)$, in which GR occurs at $v=1/2$. We show that all periodic heteroclinic chains of Bianchi type II orbits are robust for small perturbations of GR, i.e. they exist for any $v\approx 1/2$. Moreover, we prove the existence of a stable manifold for each heteroclinic chain within a Cantor set for the supercritical case, $v\in (1/2,1)$. In particular, we discuss the heteroclinic chains of periods three and four in detail.

papers.title_en: Beyond Gaussian Entanglement: Practical Criteria for Polynomially Excited Quantum States
papers.abstract_en: Polynomial excitations consisting of creation and annihilation operators are studied. Subsystem entanglement is proven produced and preserved by such manipulations. NPT entanglement already present between any two subsystems of a general pure or mixed multipartite Gaussian state is preserved under all polynomial excitations. Nevertheless, these excitations can create NPT entanglement between initially separable subsystems, implying that the number of NPT entangled pairs cannot decrease. Polynomial excitations of a wide class of initially separable pure states are considered. For these states, the method reduces the infinite-dimensional positivity problem to a finite-dimensional one: after partial transposition, NPT entanglement is equivalent to a corresponding bilinear representation matrix not being positive semi-definite. Furthermore, using symplectic diagonalization and spectral decomposition, an explicit transformation is constructed between the Fock-space and position representations. It is applied to quadratic excitations of a three-mode mixed Gaussian state. The behavior of the NPT entanglement is tracked between subsystems as a function of a parameter $κ$, which tunes the non-locality of the excitation, and quantum negativity is evaluated. Under a chosen quadratic Hamiltonian, the resulting unitary time evolution maintains NPT entanglement for long intervals, interrupted only by short periods of PPT states. Finally, a closed analytical expression is derived for the covariance matrix of a general quadratic operator for an arbitrary number of degrees of freedom in phase space. Our framework directly connects mathematical foundations, theoretical modeling, and experimentally feasible implementations.

papers.title_en: Chromatic Block-Gibbs p-Bit Decoding of QLDPC Codes
papers.abstract_en: We introduce a parallel decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes based on probabilistic bits (p-bits), tunable stochastic binary units controlled by local fields. The idea is that predicted error configurations, interpreted as explanations of the observed syndrome, are updated stochastically using local Gibbs conditionals, while a progressively strengthened parity penalty drives the search toward syndrome-valid configurations. A coloring of the decoding graph enables parallel block updates, and independent replicas and restarts provide trajectory diversity. The best candidate encountered during the search is returned, mirroring the candidate-selection strategy of recent ensemble decoders. At the stated update budgets, the resulting logical error rates are on par with leading decoders under both code-capacity and circuit-level noise. While the total number of variable resamplings can be substantially larger than the message-update count of BP-based alternatives, the numerical results establish constraint-annealed p-bit dynamics as a competitive stochastic alternative for QLDPC decoding and motivate further study of hardware-native implementations.

papers.title_en: Enhanced weak-field sensing using detuned squeezing
papers.abstract_en: Achieving measurement precision beyond the standard quantum limit (SQL) is a fundamental object in quantum metrology. In this manuscript, we propose a streamlined protocol for weak signal sensing in a trapped-ion spin-oscillator system that simultaneously exploits detuned motional squeezing and spin-oscillator entanglement.
