The data have the toroidal conformal symmetry of Beig and Husa, and a change of variable of Natanzon type reduces every mode equation to the Gauss hypergeometric equation, so that the conformal factor is a series with explicit Gamma-function coefficients. The quantities that have so far required numerical work are thereby obtained exactly. A ground-state identity gives a sharp existence criterion: complete, asymptotically flat data exist precisely for $k<k_c=0.8048016772\ldots$, and the explicit series is identified with the unique variational solution. The ADM mass is an absolutely convergent digamma series, with $m/a=πk^2/10+O(k^3)$ for small amplitudes and an explicit residue at its critical divergence. Sufficiently strong waves contain trapped surfaces: it is proved that for $k$ close to $k_c$ the rescaled conformal factor converges to an explicit function and explicit tori and spheres become outer trapped, so that the data contain an apparent horizon. A numerical search, restricted to equatorially symmetric star-shaped surfaces, finds marginally trapped (minimal) spheres, which appear in a fold near $k=0.7670$. No thin-torus or weak-field approximation is used.

papers.title_en: Entanglement Sudden Death in Gapped Ground States
papers.abstract_en: Spatial sudden death of entanglement refers to the disappearance of quantum correlations between subsystems after a certain distance called the entanglement length. Specifically, given a density matrix $ρ_{ABC}$ on a tripartite system $ABC$ with $B$ spatially separating $A$ and $C$, the entanglement length is the distance $\ell(A,C)$ after which the reduced density matrix $ρ_{AC}$, given by tracing out the $B$ subsystem, is separable. We show in the case of gapped ground states in any dimension that the entanglement length is finite on finite subsystems. Restricting to one-dimensional systems, we prove that normal matrix product states have a finite entanglement length independent of $A$ and $C$, and that a finite pure state with such uniform entanglement length has a matrix product state representation with bond dimension independent of $A$ and $C$. Consequently, in one dimension, entanglement length distinguishes matrix product states from all other pure states.

papers.title_en: Yang-Baxter deformed sigma models on $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathrm{SO}(N)$
papers.abstract_en: We study Yang--Baxter deformations of two-dimensional sigma models on compact symmetric spaces $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathrm{SO}(N)$, with particular emphasis on their ultraviolet behavior. We claim that the ultraviolet fixed point is described by the $\mathrm{SO}(N,\mathbb C)/\mathrm{SO}(N,\mathbb R)$ non-compact WZW model together with $N-1$ compact free bosons. We determine the leading correction to this fixed point and identify it with the perturbation generated by the corresponding screening currents. We also extend our construction to the broader class of symmetric spaces of maximal rank.

papers.title_en: Cyclotomic Structure and Exact Recurrences in Floquet Many-Body Quantum Dynamics
papers.abstract_en: Periodically driven quantum systems exhibit a wide range of complex dynamics, including chaos. Yet, at special parameter values, their evolution can recur exactly. Several quantum protocols have recently been proposed that exploit exact Floquet recurrences to demonstrate genuine quantum advantage. Such recurrences can be studied through the arithmetic structure of the Floquet unitary. In this work, we establish a necessary and sufficient arithmetic criterion for exact recurrence and determine the minimal recurrence period when one exists. Because recurrence is a global property of the unitary, it holds for every initial state. Applying our framework requires only knowledge of the number field associated with the Hamiltonian parameters. We demonstrate the method using the kicked Ising chain, establishing exact recurrences in both Clifford and non-Clifford regimes. We further show that, in the recurrent non-Clifford regime, magic--a resource for quantum computation--is generated at intermediate times and undergoes exact periodic revivals enforced by the recurrence of the full Floquet unitary. By connecting number theory, quantum many-body dynamics, and quantum information, our work shows that exact recurrence extends beyond Clifford circuits and opens new avenues for magic generation and quantum hardware benchmarking.

papers.title_en: Whither quantum advantage? New classical lower bounds for Max-Cut on large-girth 3-regular graphs
papers.abstract_en: Every 3-regular graph of girth at least $g$ has a cut containing at least a fraction $M_g$ of its edges, and the best rigorous bounds at large girth are $0.912\le \lim_{g\to\infty}M_g \le 0.92386$. Lower bounds on $M_g$ follow from the performance of local algorithms: on a graph of girth $g \ge 2p+2$ a depth-$p$ local algorithm sees the same tree around every edge, so its expected cut fraction on that tree bounds $M_g$ from below. We apply this strategy to the Variational Iterative Rotation Algorithm (VIRAL), a classical local algorithm, and evaluate it on the depth-$p$ tree for every even depth up to $p=32$. The resulting bounds exceed those recently obtained from the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) for every $p\ge 4$, by $0.005$ to $0.011$, and they extend the range of girths covered from $g=36$ to $g=66$. Notably, at $g=66$ we obtain $M_{66} \ge 0.9127$ at $99.99999\%$ confidence level, which raises the asymptotic lower bound from $0.912$ to $0.9127$.

papers.title_en: A Controlled Null Result for Per-Gate Riemannian Optimization in VQE
papers.abstract_en: Parametrized gates in a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) live on a product of unitary groups, which makes Riemannian optimization a natural candidate for improving training. We test this candidate in the clean per-gate setting: each single-qubit gate is optimized directly on U (2) and compared with Adam on an unconstrained Euler-angle chart representing the same physical gate, initialized from the same unitaries and tuned with a separate learning-rate sweep. On a validated hydrogen-chain benchmark, we find no measurable practical advantage from the Riemannian machinery. The direct manifold optimizer and the Euler-coordinate baseline are interleaved in final error and success rate; the classical coordinate baseline is not slower in iterations on the successful cells; and the choices of Riemannian metric, retraction, and momentum vector transport do not change the conclusion. We also identify four failure modes that can manufacture an apparent positive result: a trivial product-state benchmark, a projected-matrix Adam baseline that discards most of its own step, a non-unitary inherited Cayley retraction that lets the reported energy pass below the variational minimum, and a learning-rate grid whose optimum sits at its boundary. Each failure mode produced a plausible multi-seed result in our own workflow before being caught. The practical output of this paper is therefore a controlled null result and a validation checklist for VQE optimizer comparisons.

papers.title_en: Norm properties of quantum uniformity measures
papers.abstract_en: We prove that for $k=4$ the quantum uniformity measures are norms, whereas for every $k\geq5$ the triangle inequality fails. This gives a complete answer to an open question of Bu, Gu, and Jaffe. The $k=4$ case is proved using the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality for the quantum uniformity pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{Q^4}$ introduced here, together with the triangle inequality in a suitable finite-dimensional Bochner $L^8$ space. For $k\geq5$, we construct systems of linear equations over a finite field and derive a contradiction from the structure theory of norming linear systems.

papers.title_en: Axionic Casimir Torque
papers.abstract_en: In the canonical Casimir effect, the quantum vacuum is isotropic, and the minimization of vacuum energy drives only a linear attractive force between the plates. However, the introduction of an axion gradient breaks this rotational symmetry. It can be demonstrated that these asymmetric zero-point fluctuations exert a macroscopic mechanical twist on the plates proportional to $\vec{b}^2 \sin (2\vartheta)$ where $\vec{b}$ is the spatial axion gradient and $\vartheta$ is the angle between the axion gradient and the normal to the plates.

papers.title_en: Quasinormal modes of rotating black holes with ultralight scalar fields
papers.abstract_en: We report the first accurate computation of the leading-order shifts in the quasinormal-mode frequencies of rapidly rotating black holes surrounded by massive scalar fields with nonminimal curvature coupling. For fields with reduced Compton wavelengths no shorter than the black-hole mass scale, the numerical errors in the frequency shifts are typically $10^{-8} - 10^{-5}$ for dimensionless spins between 0 and 0.9, and at most $\mathcal{O}(10^{-3})$ next to the scalar-mass threshold. Our results open up the possibility of searching for ultralight scalar particles, prime dark-matter candidates, using existing gravitational-wave signals.

papers.title_en: How much can shape degeneracies affect the Hubble constant measurement?
papers.abstract_en: Cluster lens models are constrained almost entirely by observed lensed image positions, leaving a large space of mass perturbations with arbitrary amplitudes such that they reproduce every image exactly. Such degeneracies are known as shape degeneracies (ShaDes). We show that these ShaDes shift the observed time delays, by the difference of the perturbing potential between the two images, without depending on the number of source/lens planes. Bounding their amplitude by preserving the positivity of the convergence, image multiplicity, and parity, in MACS J0138.0$-$2155, they can contribute at least $\simeq7$ days to the delay between the detected images of SN-Encore (i.e., $17.5\%$ of the measured value of $39.8$ days) and $\simeq112$ days (i.e., $2.8$--$3.7\%$ of predicted value of $3,000-4000$ days) to the reappearance intervals predicted for SN-Encore and SN-Requiem. These error bars transfer one-to-one to $H_0$, and remain invisible in comparisons of independent models.

papers.title_en: Permanent Thermodynamic Mpemba Inversion from Quantum-Jump Feedback
papers.abstract_en: We show that a common quantum-jump feedback protocol can permanently reverse the nonequilibrium free-energy ordering of two prescribed initial states while preserving their Gibbs equilibrium. The construction exploits collective compensation between monitored channels: their feedback corrections cancel at equilibrium but remain active during relaxation. This balance preserves free-energy monotonicity while allowing the relaxation modes to be reshaped. We prove that eliminating the complete slow-sector contribution of the initially higher-free-energy state, while retaining it for the comparison state, produces distinct asymptotic decay exponents. Their free-energy ratio then vanishes at long times, guaranteeing a permanent thermodynamic quantum Mpemba inversion under the same controlled dynamics. A thermal qutrit realizes the mechanism through coherence interference and exhibits distinct detection thresholds for spectral selection and exact slow-sector cancellation under feedback retuning.

papers.title_en: Few-Magnon Universality beyond Contact Interactions in Long-Range Spin Chains
papers.abstract_en: Quantum few-body systems exhibit a rich variety of phenomena that provide fundamental insights into universality. A paradigmatic example is the Efimov effect, in which an infinite tower of three-body bound states emerges with binding energies forming a geometric sequence. Motivated by advances in trapped-ion systems, recent theoretical work has predicted that the Efimov effect can arise in certain long-range quantum spin chains, where magnons exhibit a general dispersion $ε_k=u|k|^z$ with $z\in(0.52,0.88)$ and interact through a contact potential. Nevertheless, whether Efimov universality persists in the presence of experimentally relevant long-range interactions between magnons remains unexplored. In this work, we address this issue by investigating the two- and three-magnon problems with a model interaction potential $V(x)=V_0/(1+|x|^β)$. Our results demonstrate that few-body universality persists for any $β>1$: In the two-magnon sector, the low-energy expansion of the scattering matrix near a two-body resonance agrees with the universal form predicted by contact-interaction theory. The three-magnon bound-state spectrum exhibits Efimov scaling, with a scaling factor consistent with the theory. We further highlight the experimental relevance of our model, which can be readily realized in trapped-ion systems. Our results pave the way for quantum simulations of universal few-body physics beyond the traditional paradigm of nonrelativistic particles.

papers.title_en: Adaptive Entanglement Witnessing for Two-Qubit Systems
papers.abstract_en: Entanglement witnesses are a key instrument in determining the entanglement of unknown bipartite qubit systems without requiring a full tomography. Riccardi et al. (2020) proposed a set of two-qubit witnesses, denoted $\{W^3\}$, which require a set of local measurements in three bases. In this work we propose an additional set of witnesses, denoted $\{W^5\}$, that build on $\{W^3\}$ and require measurements in two additional bases. We present an adaptive two-step method that uses the measurement results obtained for $\{W^3\}$ to select which $W^5$ to evaluate. We computationally demonstrate that our adaptive two-step protocol can identify 72% of entangled states generated according to the methods of Roik et al. (2021) while requiring measurements in only five of the nine bases needed for full quantum tomography. Additionally, we experimentally verify the behavior of both sets of witnesses using polarization-entangled photon pairs.

papers.title_en: Measuring higher-order bulk topology in a programmable quantum simulator
papers.abstract_en: Topological insulators lie outside the standard Landau paradigm: Instead of being characterized by local order parameters and spontaneous symmetry breaking, their defining properties are encoded in the global structure of their quantum states and manifested as robust boundary states. Crystalline higher-order topological insulators can extend this principle by hosting localized corner modes in two and higher dimensions. Although these boundary modes can be detected spectroscopically through the local density of states, determining the underlying bulk topology, for example through nested Wilson loops, remains an outstanding experimental challenge. Here we use up to 728 qubits in a superconducting analogue-digital quantum simulator to realize and probe a hierarchy of one-, two-, and three-dimensional topological insulators governed by effective tight-binding Hamiltonians. By reconstructing complex propagators from real-space measurements, we obtain complementary boundary and bulk characterizations: local densities of states reveal localized boundary modes, whereas experimentally reconstructed band projectors yield bulk topological invariants, culminating in a three-dimensional octupole moment extracted through third nested Wilson loops. These results establish a route to realizing, characterizing, and manipulating topologically protected states in programmable three-dimensional quantum matter.

papers.title_en: Relativistic Covariance from Hamiltonian Hydrodynamics in the Chiral Limit
papers.abstract_en: We derive the covariant equations of nondissipative chiral hydrodynamics from their equal-time Hamiltonian formulation and identify the Lie--Poisson structure implicit in the chiral brackets. This structure combines fluid motion with local chiral transformations. For a parity-invariant Hamiltonian quadratic in chiral charge densities and pion gradients, without external backgrounds, we derive and solve the constraints imposed by Lorentz boosts. Their coupled nonlinear sector is equivalent to the linear boost transformation laws of a symmetric tensor, which determine the velocity dependence from rest-frame data. For finite, positive rest-frame coefficients, finite ordinary-fluid energy density and thermodynamic derivatives, and a momentum--velocity relation that can be solved in either direction, the chiral Hamiltonian coefficients remain finite at every fluid speed below light speed if and only if the rest-frame pion propagation speed does not exceed the speed of light. This formulation makes symmetry constraints explicit and provides a starting point for future thermodynamically consistent dissipative extensions.

papers.title_en: Architectural Robustness to Label Noise Using Variational Quantum Circuits for Medical Image Classification
papers.abstract_en: Label noise is prevalent in medical image datasets, arising from observer disagreement and ambiguous cases and deep networks memorize the mislabeled examples at the cost of generalization. Current solutions such as loss correction and sample selection add training complexity and generally assume the noise rate is known or estimable. This paper investigates whether robustness can be obtained architecturally, by routing a frozen backbone's features through a low-dimensional bounded bottleneck and classifying them with a head whose function class is intrinsically smooth. Variational quantum circuits with angle encoding and a linear cost function realise exactly such a class. Their use in medical imaging, however, has been limited by the small number of qubits available on noisy intermediate-scale devices, which typically restricts inputs to low-resolution grayscale images. We therefore couple a frozen ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/16 backbone to a trainable linear bottleneck and an eight-qubit variational quantum circuit, allowing 224x224 RGB inputs to be processed. Under clean labels the model leads five of six MedMNISTv2 benchmarks against published hybrid quantum-classical models, with margins of 17.4 and 15.7 percentages on BloodMNIST and PathMNIST. The advantage emerges under corrupted labels. At symmetric noise rates of 30% and 50% the model outperforms many published quantum and noise-robust classical baselines on all six datasets without any explicit noise-handling component. Against a control that shares the backbone, bottleneck, parameter count and optimizer and replaces only the circuit with a ReLU layer, it retains 89.75% accuracy on PathMNIST at 50% noise where the control falls to 78.96%. Direct measurement of training dynamics shows that this advantage is not an inability to fit corrupted labels, which the circuit retains, but greater stability under prolonged training on them.

papers.title_en: A new AI-based Full Event Interpretation model for flavour physics
papers.abstract_en: The increasing event complexity and data rates foreseen for future LHC coinditions motivate a transition from selecting proton-proton ($pp$) collision events by reconstructing predefined signal candidates to constructing a reduced data stream by interpreting the relevant event features in a signal-agnostic way. We explore the capabilities of deep-learning-based architectures on heavy-flavour physics using LHCb as a case study. Graph-based full-event interpretation techniques address the problem by representing visible products of $pp$ collisions as nodes of a graph, and reconstructing heavy-hadron decay chains hierarchically. A new neutral-particle-aware architecture extends the input data from charged tracks to calorimeter clusters, and uses metric learning to clusterize particles from the same decay chain in a common latent space. Tests on inclusive simulated $pp\to b\bar b$ events show that this approach retains its ability to reconstruct decay chains across a broad range of topologies and multiplicities. We discuss the resulting physics opportunities, with a focus on inclusive $b\to s\ell\ell$ measurements and on searches for exotic hadrons.

papers.title_en: Sequential optimization for orbital-optimized variational quantum eigensolvers
papers.abstract_en: Orbital optimization within the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) framework is useful for improving active-space quality and accurately capturing electron correlation with shallow quantum circuits. The orbital-optimized unitary coupled cluster (OO-UCC) method [W. Mizukami et al., Phys. Rev. Res. 2, 033421 (2020)], in its original formulation, employs the orbital gradient and Hessian in a Newton--Laphson procedure. In this study, we propose sequential orbital-optimized unitary coupled cluster doubles (SOO-UCCD), extending the gradient-free sequential minimal optimization approach [K. M. Nakanishi et al., Phys. Rev. Res. 2, 043158 (2020)] to orbital rotation parameters. Based on the frequency structure implied by the algebraic properties of the orbital rotation generators, our method determines each orbital rotation angle from a nine-point energy profile. The energy landscape is evaluated by classically transforming the Hamiltonian integrals and contracting them with the reduced density matrices already measured for the VQE energy evaluation. This allows for orbital optimization without evaluating the orbital gradient or Hessian. By building on the core benefits of the OO-UCC framework, our method provides a gradient-free and hyperparameter-free orbital-optimization procedure. State-vector simulations for LiH in the STO-3G basis show that SOO-UCCD reproduces UCCSD-level accuracy along the bond-stretching curve and exhibits macro-iteration convergence comparable to that of L-BFGS-based orbital optimization.

papers.title_en: Collective Floquet engineering between two distant superconducting artificial atoms
papers.abstract_en: A one-dimensional waveguide is a crucial medium for transferring propagating quantum information between remote qubits, yet the photon-mediated interaction is typically fixed by the static device geometry, qubit parameters, and their couplings to the transmission line. Such an interaction can be engineered to be coherent or dissipative via virtual- or real-photon exchange, respectively, yet its effective strength remains fixed in either case. Here we demonstrate dynamical control over this interaction by applying Floquet engineering to two superconducting qubits coupled to a waveguide terminated by a capacitive mirror. By positioning one qubit at an antinode and the other qubit at a node or an antinode of the resonant standing wave, we realize a Hermitian or non-Hermitian coupling between the two qubits. A periodic flux drive of the qubit frequencies then enables on-demand control of the coherent energy splitting and the collective decay. Our results establish Floquet engineering as a route to dynamically reshape both coherent and dissipative photon-mediated interactions between remote quantum emitters.

papers.title_en: Radiation-Regulated Spherical Accretion with an Inner Accretion Disk
papers.abstract_en: We develop a theoretical model for radiation-regulated spherical accretion with an inner accretion disk. In our model, the outer accretion flow remains quasi-spherical and optically thick, while the luminosity generated by the inner disk is self-consistently coupled to the accretion rate and irradiates the inflowing gas. By solving the global transonic structure with radiative transfer treated in the diffusion approximation, we investigate how radiation regulates the flow structure and the accretion rate. We find that the luminosity is constrained by a generalized Eddington limit, leading to a saturated accretion rate typically lower than the classical Bondi prediction by orders of magnitude. At sufficiently low densities, the enthalpy flux of the spherical inflow contributes substantially to the emergent luminosity, in which case the inner disk luminosity is reduced and the accretion flow enters an unsaturated state. A criterion is derived to estimate whether the accretion flow is saturated. We further demonstrate the applicability of our model by considering fallback accretion in failed supernova systems. The predicted nearly constant emergent luminosity, constrained by the generalized Eddington limit, provides a possible explanation for the observed luminosity plateau in the failed supernova candidate M31-2014-DS1. The presence of an inner disk also provides sufficient radiation to avoid the under-luminous predictions of a purely spherical fallback model extending down to the central object. Our model provides a framework for studying radiation-regulated accretion flows in systems where low but finite angular momentum leads to the formation of an accretion disk within a larger-scale quasi-spherical inflow.

papers.title_en: Multipolar Nanophotonics with Quantum Computers
papers.abstract_en: Small particles respond to light through electric and magnetic patterns called multipoles. Their interference determines the direction of scattered light and affects the decay of nearby emitters. Larger nanoantenna arrays, metasurfaces, and other nanophotonic systems demand increasingly costly simulations to meet strict performance and reliability requirements. We show how to represent these responses with quantum bits (qubits) and use quantum circuits to calculate scattering and the Purcell effect, the change in an emitter's decay rate caused by its surroundings. The circuits can encode known multipoles or estimate unknown ones from Maxwell's equations at the particle surface. We test the method against classical theory using an ideal quantum simulator and real IBM and IonQ quantum computers. For a silicon nanoparticle of radius 78 nm illuminated at 679 nm, IonQ gives a forward directivity of 2.984, close to the ideal dipolar value 3, quantifying the concentration of scattered light in the forward direction. For an emitter 10 nm from a gold nanoparticle and emitting at 510 nm, IBM measurements yield a calculated total decay rate 20.48 times its vacuum value versus 20.47 from theory, with correction for errors in reading the qubit states. We also establish how the number of multipoles and the required accuracy set the demands on qubits and measurements. These results motivate quantum-assisted design studies of directional radiation and emitter decay in nanophotonic systems.

papers.title_en: QIAP: A Quantum-Inspired Authentication Protocol with BB84-Based Channel Monitoring
papers.abstract_en: Authentication in quantum-aware communication settings requires mechanisms that verify user legitimacy while also assessing whether the communication channel exhibits excessive disturbance. This paper presents QIAP, a stateful hybrid framework that combines classical commitment-based challenge-response authentication with BB84-based quantum-channel monitoring. QIAP uses a dual-branch verification structure inspired by rectilinear and diagonal basis selection. In the rectilinear branch, the prover opens a hash-based commitment and the verifier checks consistency with the registered round token. In the diagonal branch, the prover returns an HMAC tag bound to the verifier nonce, round identifier, and submitted commitment without disclosing the round-specific sub-secret. Under the stated hash, HMAC, freshness, secure-registration, protected-storage, and high-entropy-secret assumptions, QIAP provides computational resistance to the modeled wrong-secret and replay attempts and protects the long-term master secret from direct recovery. After successful authentication, the BB84 module estimates the quantum bit error rate (QBER) and aborts the session when the measured value reaches or exceeds the configured threshold. In the reported simulation, no successful authentication was observed among 1,000 tested wrong-secret attempts per branch. The baseline and full intercept-resend conditions produced mean QBER values of approximately 0.02 and 0.25, respectively. The classical authentication stage required approximately 0.6 ms, and the implemented authentication messages required approximately 113 bytes per round. These results indicate that QIAP can provide a lightweight hybrid framework for combining secret-based identity verification with QBER-based channel-disturbance assessment under the stated threat model.

papers.title_en: Spiral galaxy spacetime in extended scalar-tensor-Gauss-Bonnet gravity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics
papers.abstract_en: In this work, using nonlinear electrodynamics (NLED) as a source in the field equations of extended scalar-tensor-Gauss-Bonnet (E-STGB) gravity, a novel type of static and spherically symmetric spacetime is found. We show that this novel type of spacetime can be used to explain the rotation curves and gravitational lensing of spiral galaxies. The NLED model used to derive our solution, in the weak and strong field limits, reduces to Maxwell electrodynamics. Furthermore, for a wide range of parameter values where our solution describes the gravitational field of a spiral galaxy, the NLED model satisfies the null and weak energy conditions. Hence, our results suggest that the extended scalar-tensor-Gauss-Bonnet gravity minimally coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics (E-STGB-NLED) provides a viable alternative to explain flat rotation curves of spiral galaxies without invoking dark matter.

papers.title_en: A Low-Temperature Tool for Acousto-electric Detection
papers.abstract_en: We have developed an apparatus for the measurement of the acousto-electric effect (AEE) from room temperature to liquid nitrogen temperatures. The AEE is excited by bulk acoustic waves (BAWs) for which a lithium niobate piezoelectric actuator is employed. A very low background noise level is realized through careful electrical and mechanical design of the setup. The validity of the setup is tested by measuring the AEE in heavily doped P-type and N-type silicon. The opposite sign of the AEE signal was seen for both samples, showing dependence of the signal on the type of charge carrier being dragged by acoustic waves. The signal showed quadratic dependence on the driving voltage, which is consistent with the AEE literature. Further, a temperature dependence of the AEE signal was measured, which exhibits a monotonic increase with a rise in temperature. The ability to probe the AEE in bulk samples at low temperatures makes this setup a promising tool to investigate the AEE and related phenomena in different materials at cryogenic temperatures.

papers.title_en: Perfect discrimination of an orthogonal $2\otimes2$ basis may require collective separable measurements on two copies
papers.abstract_en: We consider an orthogonal basis of $\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^2$ with three entangled states and one product state. This basis is not perfectly distinguishable by LOCC or even by separable measurements when a single copy of the unknown state is available. We show that with two copies no adaptive separable protocol, which measures the copies one at a time, distinguishes the basis perfectly. We then show that a collective separable measurement on the two copies does. Whether two copies suffice for LOCC remains open.

papers.title_en: Noise-resistant off-resonance π-rotation realized in an NMR system
papers.abstract_en: Precise manipulation of qubits (spins) requires strong suppression of noise arising from couplings between qubits and their environment, as well as from driving field fluctuations. We propose a double-pulse sequence and an eighteen-pulse sequence to realize a single spin pi-rotation under off-resonance conditions (instead of conventional on-resonance or near-resonance conditions). It is proved that the latter sequence performs much better than the former in simultaneously suppressing both dephasing and driving field noise. As a proof of principle, we experimentally demonstrate, by implementing both sequences in an NMR spin system with a polarized initial spin state, that the off-resonance pi-rotation fidelity reaches as high as 0.9992 +/- 0.0008 for the double-pulse sequence and 0.9997 +/- 0.0006 for the eighteen-pulse sequence. In addition, the noise-tolerance range of the eighteen-pulse sequence is about 20 percent of the driving field strength, approximately three times wider than that of the double-pulse sequence. Besides its potential application in the NMR community, our proposal provides an alternative practical way to accurately control qubits by suppressing the coexisting transversal and longitudinal noises.

papers.title_en: Quantitative upper bounds for certain quantum channel divergences
papers.abstract_en: We show that completely positive maps can be decomposed into sums of submaps which are close in completely bounded trace norm but as far apart as possible in terms of geometric channel fidelity. We then show that this kind of behavior extends to a large class of quantum channel divergences. We construct quantitative norm estimates for quantum channel divergences in terms of the Arveson-Radon-Nikodym theorem.

papers.title_en: Detectability of 21-cm Power Spectra from the Epoch of Reionization using Modern Radio Telescopes
papers.abstract_en: One of the unsolved questions in astrophysics and cosmology is the development of a robust physical model to explain the thermal history of the intergalactic medium during the epoch of reionization. Various astrophysical models have been proposed, but current models remain only partially constrained by available observations. To clarify this ambiguity, hydrodynamical, semi-numerical, and N-body simulations can help solve this issue. One notable simulation from the epoch of reionization is the 21SSD simulations, which provide high-resolution results for the global 21-cm brightness temperature and the 21-cm power spectrum during the epoch of reionization. The simulation includes 45 models spanning three key astrophysical parameters of X-ray emissivity, Lyman-band emissivity, and the X-ray hard-to-soft emissivity ratio. Distinct values of these parameters result in different models of this simulation. In this work, four active radio observatories, including HERA, MWA, GMRT, and LOFAR have been considered to investigate the sensitivity and thermal noise of the 21-cm power spectrum. Each observatory has a particular sensitivity based on its instrumental characteristics, which helps assess which models lie above the forecast sensitivity thresholds of current instruments.

papers.title_en: Deterministic preparation of squeezed and non-Gaussian states in coupled qubit-boson systems
papers.abstract_en: Deterministic preparation of bosonic resource states is a central task in continuous-variable quantum information processing and quantum metrology. Here we develop a measurement-based imaginary time evolution (MITE) protocol for preparing squeezed and non-Gaussian states. The protocol combines ancilla-mediated weak measurements of the Hamiltonian with a conditional phase rotation that suppresses excited state trapping and stabilizes convergence toward the ground state. The method is potentially applicable in hybrid discrete variable-continuous variable (DV-CV) platforms, where the qubit acts as the measurement readout. We demonstrate deterministic convergence over a broad range of parameters and show that the performance degradation near the stability boundary is governed by the shrinking Bogoliubov quasiparticle gap. The same framework also extends to non-Gaussian bosonic resource states, including Schrödinger cat states and excited states of the single-mode squeezing Hamiltonian, which display Wigner negativity. The squeezed states remain robust under bosonic loss over experimentally relevant regimes.

papers.title_en: Equation of State Classification of Core-Collapse Supernovae with a Network of Gravitational-Wave Detectors
papers.abstract_en: Gravitational waves from core-collapse supernovae may provide a unique probe of the equation of state (EOS) of dense nuclear matter. In previous work, we assessed the potential of machine-learning methods for EOS classification for rapidly rotating supernovae using individual gravitational-wave detectors. Here, we extend the framework to detector networks and investigate the impact of detector configuration, source distance, arrival time, and sky location on the classification. Using convolutional neural networks, we perform 10-class EOS classification directly from noisy detector data for both second- and third-generation observatories. We find that detector geometry strongly influences classification performance. For Galactic events, current detector networks can achieve promising classification performance, but the reach depends sensitively on the detector network antenna response. Adding detectors improves time-averaged performance and produces more uniform classification across the sky. Third-generation observatories extend the classification reach to 100 kpc for favorable source orientations but do not remove the dependence on detector geometry.

papers.title_en: Minimal Subsystems for Characterizing Genuine Multipartite Entanglement
papers.abstract_en: Genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) is a valuable resource for quantum technologies, but quantifying it in many-body systems can be demanding since measures defined through optimizations over bipartitions are often assumed to require large joint measurements and many measurement settings. We introduce the concepts of GME evaluation length and GME evaluation number, which capture, respectively, the largest subsystem that must be jointly measured and the number of distinct subsystems that need to be measured to evaluate multipartite entanglement measures defined via bipartition optimizations. Taking the genuine multipartite concurrence (GMC) as a canonical example, we show that, for $N$-qubit Haar-random pure states, the GMC can be evaluated using only $N$ single-qubit purity measurements. Thus, for typical many-body states, evaluating the GMC requires considering only the $N$ single-site bipartitions, rather than the exponentially many distinct bipartitions. We further corroborate this behavior numerically for physically accessible states generated by local random quantum circuits. Our results show that the practical cost of quantifying GME can be dramatically lower than suggested by its formal definition, establishing measurement complexity as a complementary operational lens for multipartite entanglement.

papers.title_en: Time-Frequency Continuous-Variable Quantum Teleportation with Single Photons
papers.abstract_en: Quantum teleportation, a key building block for quantum technologies, enables distant parties, Alice and Bob, to transfer an unknown quantum state using entanglement, local operations, and classical communication. In this work, we propose a quantum teleportation protocol for single-photon time-frequency continuous variables, where time is the time of arrival at a detector. We detail the operational requirements of the protocol, notably the nonlinear interactions needed for the photon-photon time-frequency entangling gate. By explicitly treating the detector position as the reference frame for time of arrival, we show that, even with ideal classical and quantum channels, the input-output fidelity is not unity unless the receiving party can correct the detector-position mismatch. This results in a trade-off between teleportation fidelity and the temporal bandwidth of the input photon wavepacket. The protocol itself can be used for remote detector synchronization. In particular, we show that time-frequency cat and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states provide an internal temporal ruler through fidelity revivals. We further derive the classical and best-copy fidelity thresholds for single-photon Gaussian wavepackets, finding that the relevant vacuum-equivalent shot noise is input-dependent, in contrast with quadrature-based continuous-variable quantum teleportation. Our proposal derives from a quantum theory of space-time events, whereafter we establish space as a reference for the time degree of freedom, thereby grounding our work in ongoing research on reference frames and superselection rules in quantum optics and quantum information. Beyond protocols harnessing time-frequency continuous variables of single photons, this work points toward remote synchronization in quantum communication architectures.

papers.title_en: Probing LZ-Motivated TeV Higgsino Dark Matter through Heavier Sparticles at LHC
papers.abstract_en: The nearly pure TeV-scale Higgsino dark matter provides a natural explanation for the high-energy nuclear-recoil excess reported by LUX-ZEPLIN. Such a heavy and compressed Higgsino spectrum makes direct searches at the LHC challenging. We therefore investigate complementary probes through the production and decay of heavier sparticles. We perform a comprehensive analysis and obtain the following observations: (i) For a TeV Higgsino, the current LHC Run-2 searches exclude gluino up to approximately 2.2~TeV, while the HL-LHC can give an exclusion reach of 2.5--2.6~TeV and a discovery reach of 2.3--2.4~TeV; (ii) The light-flavor squark coannihilation window lies beyond the Run-2 reach, but its lower end could be excluded at the HL-LHC under optimistic assumptions; (iii) The Run-2 search does not exclude the stop or sbottom benchmarks; (iv) The slepton and heavier-electroweakino productions are too small to access at the HL-LHC.

papers.title_en: Letter of Intent for Alpha Knockout from Nuclei in Hard Exclusive Processes with ALERT
papers.abstract_en: We propose to measure hard exclusive $α$-knockout reactions from the light $α$-conjugate nuclei $^{12}$C, $^{16}$O, and $^{20}$Ne using electron scattering. Three reaction channels will be measured for the first time on the same target set: (i) the quasi-elastic knockout $(e, e' α)$ knockout, which establishes a baseline against $α$-clustering model calculations and tests final-state-interaction (FSI) models; (ii) coherent deeply virtual Compton scattering (DVCS) on a bound $α$, which provides a quark-level probe of the bound system through the beam-spin asymmetry; and (iii) coherent vector-meson production ($ϕ$ and J/{$ψ$}) on a bound $α$, which probes the gluon distribution of the bound cluster through two-gluon exchange. The central observables are ratios of cross sections and beam-spin asymmetries between the bound $α$ in $^{12}$C, $^{16}$O, and $^{20}$ Ne and the free $^4$He ground state. Together these measurements directly address the question of the role of QCD in the structure of light nuclei : do the quark and gluon distributions of an $α$ embedded in a heavier nucleus differ from those of a free 4He, and do those modifications track the increasing $α$-clustering strength along the $α$-conjugate chain? The measurement will use the 12 GeV CEBAF accelerator in Hall B with the CLAS12 spectrometer instrumented with the ALERT low-energy recoil detector and high-pressure gas straw targets. ALERT, which replaced the CLAS12 silicon vertex tracker, was successfully commissioned and operated during Run Group L (RG-L) from April through August 2025. It uniquely provides identification of low-momentum recoiling light ions (p, d, t, $^3$He, and $^4$He) close to the beamline at the high luminosities required by these exclusive channels.

papers.title_en: Direct Observational Constraint on Upstream Magnetic Field Amplification Reveals the Particle Acceleration Limit in a Supernova Remnant
papers.abstract_en: The origin of Galactic cosmic rays up to the knee energy (PeV) remains a long-standing open question in astrophysics. Supernova remnant shocks are leading candidates for accelerating particles to PeV energies, yet this requires strong magnetic field amplification in the upstream region to confine the highest energy particles. Despite its importance, the upstream magnetic field strength has long lacked direct observational constraints. Here we report the observation of numerous synchrotron X-ray hotspots extending into the upstream of the supernova remnant RX J1713.7$-$3946 in archival Chandra data. These hotspots show spatial and temporal properties consistent with synchrotron emission from secondary electrons produced by hadronic interactions between accelerated protons and dense molecular clumps. Using the spatial extent of these upstream hotspots as a physical scale, we estimate the proton diffusion length to be $\sim 1~\mathrm{pc}$. This measurement provides a constraint on the upstream magnetic field strength of $\sim 10~μ\mathrm{G}$, which is consistent with recent simulations of Bell-instability-driven magnetic field amplification. Our results indicate that the current amplification is insufficient to reach PeV energies, explaining the observed TeV gamma-ray spectral cutoff and providing a diagnostic for assessing PeVatron capability in stellar shocks.

papers.title_en: Retarded Green Function For Bopp--Podolsky Electrodynamics in Four-Dimensional De Sitter Spacetime
papers.abstract_en: We study classical Bopp--Podolsky (BP) electrodynamics on four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime, focusing on its transverse retarded Green function and gauge-invariant electromagnetic response. Because de Sitter spacetime is maximally symmetric, its vector Green functions admit a covariant expansion in a finite basis of invariant bitensors, with scalar coefficients depending only on the invariant separation. For conserved sources, the fourth-order field operator factorizes into Maxwell and massive-vector operators, yielding the BP retarded kernel as the difference of their transverse Green functions. Using the invariant bitensor decomposition, we reduce the propagator equations to a hypergeometric master equation and determine the distributional structure of its solution. The common leading short-distance singularity of the Maxwell and massive-vector sectors cancels, leaving a logarithmic master singularity and a softened vector-potential wavefront. After one curl, the gauge-invariant field-strength kernel contains a null-cone delta distribution and a regular timelike tail. The smooth Maxwell master tail is annihilated by the curl, so the interior electromagnetic tail is generated entirely by the massive sector. We also derive an exact horizon-regular static potential, demonstrate the cancellation of the Coulomb divergence, recover the flat-space BP potential, and formulate the generalized Gauss law. On global de Sitter spacetime, the compactness of the spatial sections requires the total charge to vanish; we implement this constraint using an antipodal charge configuration with smooth factorized initial data. The analysis is classical and does not assume a quantum Lee--Wick contour or a preferred de Sitter vacuum.

papers.title_en: Asteroseismology of Neutron Stars with Axion-Like Particle Mediated Dark Matter
papers.abstract_en: We examine the impacts of dark matter (DM) on the observables of the neutron star (NS). The interaction of DM with nucleons intermediate by axion-like particles (ALPs), and the DM-admixed NS (DNS) is formulated in the framework of the relativistic mean field (RMF) formalism. The effects of the DM on the NS are characterized by two parameters: DM Fermi momentum ($q_f$) and DM mass ($m_χ$). By varying these two parameters, we investigate how the NS's mass, radius, and tidal deformability are altered. Furthermore, we study how the ALP-mediated DM impacts the stability of the NS through the analysis of radial oscillations. In addition, the nonradial oscillation has been investigated by calculating its fundamental mode frequency in the DNS and analyzed how the ALP-mediated DM modifies its behavior.

papers.title_en: Nonequilibrium framework for first-order phase transitions
papers.abstract_en: The first-order phase transition is central to electroweak baryogenesis and gravitational wave generation, yet thermal equilibrium effective potential analyses cannot describe the real-time non-equilibrium dynamics of the phase transition process. We use the Schwinger-Keldysh closed-time-path formalism of real-time finite-temperature field theory to study these effects. For the $ϕ^6$ model, we derive the effective action and the corresponding Langevin equation. We further extend the formalism to the two scalar fields case, obtaining the coupled Langevin equations. These results provide a theoretical framework for the bubble nucleation simulation of the non-equilibrium phase transition process, laying the foundation for reliable predictions of baryogenesis and gravitational wave signals.

papers.title_en: Metasurface quantum graphs for polarization-independent certified randomness
papers.abstract_en: Quantum random number generators are crucial for information security, yet existing implementations are hindered by bulky optics, device imperfections, and state alignment constraints. Here, using a compact metasurface platform, we achieve polarization-independent certified randomness by establishing a quantitative quantum graph framework. By mapping multi-channel nanophotonic responses onto graph vertices, we assign metasurface measurements an operational information-theoretic meaning, directly connecting weighted graph degrees to conditional min-entropy estimation. The resulting graph-certified measurements yield robust private randomness even under entanglement-based attacks without complex optics. Experimentally, we fabricate 4- and 6-channel dielectric metasurfaces to implement high-dimensional positive operator-valued measure graphs, successfully certifying randomness with heralded single photons and Poissonian light. By integrating complex quantum measurements into a single passive layer, our metasurface quantum graphs provide a scalable route for integrated quantum technologies.

papers.title_en: Entanglement and parametric resonance in coupled oscillator systems
papers.abstract_en: We study a system of two quadratically-coupled harmonic oscillators, prepared respectively in the ground state and in a coherent state. This toy model can describe for instance the dynamics of one mode of a quantum field evolving in a harmonically-oscillating classical background. In such situations, it is well-known that, depending on the background oscillation amplitude and coupling strength, the system may exhibit parametric resonance. Using the Feynman-Vernon influence functional, we analyze the interplay between parametric resonance and quantum entanglement by perturbatively computing the purity of the mixed state resulting from tracing over one of the oscillators. We find a runaway behavior of the quantum entanglement between the two oscillators, as well as a rapid breakdown of the validity of perturbation theory, in regions of parametric instability. This provides a quantitative confirmation of various statements in the literature and is highly relevant to questions pertaining to the validity of the semiclassical approximation in coupled quantum-classical systems.

papers.title_en: Sensitivity of calibration-free DESI DR2 BAO--supernova constraints to a distance-duality tilt
papers.abstract_en: Recent measurements from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) have reported a moderate preference for dynamical dark energy, challenging the standard $Λ$CDM paradigm. Nonetheless, such a trend could reflect a tension between the shape and the offset of the Hubble diagrams predicted by current BAO and Type Ia supernovae (SN) data, which may underpin a possible breakdown of the cosmic distance duality relation (CDDR) linking luminosity distances $D_{\rm L}$ and angular-diameter distances $D_{\rm A}$. We explore this possibility by parametrizing deviations from this relation as $η(z) \equiv D_{\rm L} / [{(1+z)}^2 D_{\rm A}] = α{(1+z)}^\varepsilon$, and investigate how the preference for a Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) dynamical dark energy is modified once $\varepsilon \!\neq\! 0$ is allowed. Using DESI DR2 and uncalibrated SN data (Pantheon$+$, DES-Dovekie, Union3, and Union3.1), we find that allowing $\varepsilon$ to vary freely in both $Λ$CDM and CPL reduces the CPL preference with respect to $Λ$CDM by a larger amount than the addition of spatial curvature $Ω_k$; only Union3.1 exhibits comparable reductions. We also find that the preference reduction is robust to alternative $η(z)$ parametrizations, and that the $η(z)$ constraints remain stable under the removal of BAO tracers or low-redshift cutoffs for Pantheon$+$, whereas the DES-Dovekie preference largely disappears once $z < 0.1$ SN are removed. In a separate calibrated analysis, illustrative Planck sound-horizon and SH0ES absolute-magnitude priors give $α\simeq 0.942 \pm 0.014$, quantifying the normalization mismatch under those assumptions. We also map the CDDR violation onto photon-loss and varying-$G$ scenarios, concluding that the cosmological constraints are much weaker than existing constraints on these physical mechanisms.

papers.title_en: Device-to-protocol simulation of spectrally-resolved quantum photonic circuits
papers.abstract_en: Predicting quantum-photonic circuit performance requires retaining source and device physics without making photon-counting calculations prohibitively expensive. Here we present PhoQuS, a framework that combines frequency-resolved source models, electromagnetic compact models and spatially correlated fabrication variation to simulate quantum photonic circuits. Covariance-Gram reduction after full-resolution Gaussian propagation lowers readout cost while retaining dominant spectral correlations. For continuous-variable state preparation, spectral reduction accelerates photon counting by 60.4-fold in an approximate Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill circuit. Frequency-resolved modeling guides the use of cascaded squeezing with temporal walk-off compensation, yielding 0.99 fidelity to the single-mode circuit reference and 0.98 conditional purity in lossless simulations. For discrete-variable state preparation, simulations of three-photon Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger circuits across a virtual wafer show that component robustness alone does not predict circuit fidelity, which depends jointly on source spectra, circuit architecture and control. PhoQuS connects device physics to protocol-level performance through a unified workflow that retains spectral detail while reducing readout cost.

papers.title_en: Universal Boolean Computation in Negatively Coupled Circle Map Lattices
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the computational capabilities of a one-dimensional lattice of negatively coupled circle maps in its traveling wave regime. We interpret propagating waves as information carriers and exploit their interactions to implement Boolean logic. The logical states are encoded by the propagation direction of the traveling waves, while the presence or absence of a wave at a designated output location represents the logical output. Using controlled wave collisions, we demonstrate the realization of NAND and NOR gates along with other basic gates. Since NAND and NOR operations are functionally complete, the results establish that the traveling wave regime of the negatively coupled circle-map lattice supports universal Boolean computation in principle. The demonstrated logical operations remain valid over a finite range of the coupling strength εand map parameter ω, indicating robustness of the computational scheme to parameter variations. Our results therefore demonstrate that computational functionality can emerge from the collective nonlinear dynamics of a coupled map lattice, providing a con- nection between the dynamical properties of traveling wave states and collision based information processing.

papers.title_en: Bell's go theorem: regaining local causality with a new notion of realism
papers.abstract_en: Bell's theorem is popularly stated as the inconsistency of quantum theory with local realism. Realism is here formalized by the ontological models framework, where elements of reality are points of a measurable space and probabilities obey the Kolmogorov axioms. In the Bell scenario, locally causal ontological models posit a common cause supporting a global valuation, a joint assignment of outcomes to all measurements at once, across incompatible contexts. Within this notion of realism, Bell's theorem makes any realist explanation of the quantum predictions conspiratorial: any mechanism, whether superluminal, superdeterministic, or retrocausal, must be finely tuned so as never to manifest operationally. We redefine realism through a new ontological framework that generalizes the standard one. The elements of reality, which we call records, are no longer points but relational parts of a point-free generalization of a topological space (sublocales of a locale). A record shared by two incompatible contexts establishes the sameness of a measurement across them, without such pairwise identities composing into a global valuation, and the common cause is then a web of such records. Within this framework, Bell's no-go theorem becomes a go theorem: local causality, restated for records, is no longer at odds with the quantum statistics. This is possible because modularity, the inclusion-exclusion law of classical probability, fails across incompatible contexts, so that the probability theory generalizes Kolmogorov's. We exhibit explicit models reproducing several quantum strategies, including the optimal CHSH violation. More broadly, locally causal models of this kind attain every Bell-CHSH value up to the algebraic maximum. A realist explanation of the quantum predictions need not be conspiratorial; every causal influence posited by these models is reflected in the operational predictions.

papers.title_en: Magic-Free Certification of Logical Error Rates in Universal Fault-Tolerant Circuits
papers.abstract_en: As quantum hardware enters the fault-tolerant regime, algorithms are beginning to be executed on encoded qubits, yet scalable certification of how well they run remains an open problem. Here we introduce magic-free certification, a certification protocol for universal fault-tolerant circuits that consumes no magic, the resource that generally places them beyond efficient classical simulation and is by far the most expensive element of a fault-tolerant computation. The protocol is code- and decoder-agnostic, runs interleaved with the target circuit on the same device, and has a sample complexity that grows linearly with the number of logical qubits and non-Clifford gates while remaining decoupled from the logical error rate itself. Given a predefined error tolerance $p_L^*$, the protocol determines at a chosen confidence level whether the device executes the target circuit at a logical error rate below $p_L^*$. The method relies on trap circuits, copies of the target with every magic state replaced by a stabilizer state, whose outcomes are deterministic and which, being indistinguishable from the target to stochastic Pauli noise, fail at the same rate. We illustrate the protocol in Steane-code simulations of a magic state injection gadget and a quantum Fourier transform.

papers.title_en: Experimental Demonstration of Soft-Tissue Muon Scattering Tomography
papers.abstract_en: Muons have fascinated physicists since their discovery in cosmic rays almost a century ago. Their large mass and relatively long lifetime allow relativistic muons to traverse large amounts of matter, a property that has been exploited to probe otherwise inaccessible structures, from volcanoes and archaeological monuments to shielded nuclear materials. Here, we experimentally demonstrate for the first time that muon scattering tomography can be extended to biological soft tissue. We image an anthropomorphic thorax phantom using a 2 GeV/c muon beam at the CERN Proton Synchrotron and reconstruct its three-dimensional scattering density from the measured deflections of individual muons. Despite the weak scattering produced by tissue-equivalent materials, the reconstructed density agrees with the expectation from simulation at the percent level. Our results extend muon imaging into a previously unexplored regime and open the possibility of using muons as a complementary probe for medical imaging.

papers.title_en: Benchmarking a randomized quantum algorithm for estimating expectation values of molecular observables
papers.abstract_en: Randomized quantum algorithms for the estimation of expectation values of molecular observables offer a promising route to early fault-tolerant quantum advantage by trading circuit depth for an increased number of samples. However, this begs the question whether the resulting measurement overhead remains feasible for industrially relevant molecular systems. In this work, we benchmark the randomized sampling algorithm of Wang et al. [1] through numerical simulations on a hydrogen molecule and resource estimates for various active spaces of the cytochrome P450, an industry-relevant system in the pharmaceutical industry. Our numerical simulations reveal that the analytical error bounds significantly overestimate the actual sampling error, whereas the analytical bound on the required imaginary evolution time is comparatively tight, exceeding a direct DMRG estimate by roughly 44% for the active space where the comparison is feasible. The measurement overhead nevertheless remains prohibitively high: even for the smallest active spaces, the expectation-value estimation alone requires around 1010 samples, scaling to beyond 1015 for the largest active spaces considered. These results suggest that substantial improvements in measurement strategies or algorithmic scaling are necessary before randomized early-fault-tolerant algorithms become competitive for industrial quantum chemistry applications.

papers.title_en: Probing first-generation doublet vector-like leptons via single production at the 3 TeV CLIC
papers.abstract_en: The single production of first-generation $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ doublet vector-like leptons (VLLs) at the Compact Linear Collider (CLIC) with $\sqrt{s}=3~\mathrm{TeV}$ is studied. The neutral and charged VLL states are investigated through $e^+e^-\rightarrowν_e\bar N+\barν_eN$ and $e^+e^-\rightarrow e^\pm E^\mp$, respectively. The neutral VLL is searched for in the $N\rightarrow W^\mp e^\pm$ channel with $W^\pm\rightarrow jj$, leading to the $e^\pm+2j+\slashed{E}_T$ final state. The charged VLL is explored through $E^\pm\rightarrow e^\pm h$ ($h\rightarrow b\bar b$) and $E^\pm\rightarrow e^\pm Z$ ($Z\rightarrow q\bar q$), yielding the $e^+e^-+2b$ and $e^+e^-+2j$ signatures. Signal and background simulations include initial-state radiation, beamstrahlung, and detector effects. Cut-based analyses are performed for integrated luminosities of $1$, $3$, and $5~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$ to obtain the exclusion and discovery sensitivities in the VLL mass--mixing parameter space. The neutral-VLL channel gives the best sensitivity. At $1~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, the $2σ$ exclusion reaches $\varepsilon\simeq0.013$ at $M_N=1.3~\mathrm{TeV}$ and $\varepsilon\simeq0.065$ at $M_N=2.9~\mathrm{TeV}$, while the $5σ$ discovery reach corresponds to $\varepsilon\simeq0.02$--$0.10$. At $5~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, the charged-VLL channels probe masses up to about $2.9~\mathrm{TeV}$ and $2.8~\mathrm{TeV}$ in the $e^\pm h$ and $e^\pm Z$ modes, respectively. These results demonstrate that a 3 TeV CLIC can provide sensitive probes of first-generation doublet VLLs over a wide mass range, including scenarios with small VLL--electron mixing.

papers.title_en: Representation dependence of the neutron-proton kinetic energy in adiabatic deuteron stripping
papers.abstract_en: The adiabatic distorted-wave approximation (ADWA), the standard model for deuteron stripping and pickup, depends on the neutron-proton interaction through the form factor $V_{np}ϕ_d$. With nonlocal nucleon potentials, the neutron-proton kinetic energy averaged with this form factor shifts the energy at which the nucleon-target potentials are evaluated, and ADWA cross sections become sensitive to the choice of interaction. I ask whether this sensitivity reflects short-range neutron-proton structure. A unitary transformation of the neutron-proton Hamiltonian with the AV18 interaction, confined to short distances, represents the same interaction differently and preserves the two-body scattering matrix, the deuteron binding energy, and both asymptotic normalizations. It raises the weighted kinetic energy from 218 to 313 MeV, a change equal to more than half the range spanned by the five realistic interactions studied, while the finite-range coefficient, which controls low-momentum transfer, hardly moves. The weighted kinetic energy is dominated by the variance of the kinetic energy, which the high-momentum components control, whereas the finite-range coefficient is set by the spatial extent of the form factor. A dependence on $V_{np}$ carried by the weighted kinetic energy can therefore arise from the representation of the interaction alone, and does not by itself measure its short-range content.

papers.title_en: From Earth to Mars and Beyond: AI-Driven Cosmic-Ray Validation and Prediction with CorsikaAgent
papers.abstract_en: We calculate the sea-level cosmic-ray muon flux with CORSIKA and develop CorsikaAgent, an auditable large-language-model-based system for configuring, executing, and validating air-shower simulations, and for predicting particle fluxes in unexplored environments. The physics calculation uses proton primaries described by the solar-minimum spectrum of Papini et al., with UrQMD at low interaction energies and either Sibyll 2.3e or QGSJET-III at high energies. The predicted momentum spectra at approximately 0 and 75 degrees are compared with experimental measurements of the atmospheric muon flux and with commonly used analytic parametrizations. The two interaction-model configurations give similar spectra and describe the principal momentum and zenith-angle dependences of the data. The agent independently reconstructs the same observable through a different sampling strategy and keeps every steering card, executable, seed, log, and analysis script bound to the result it produced; its output is consistent with the direct calculation at the level resolved by the present comparison. Transferred to Mars, the workflow reproduces the CORSIKA 8 benchmark, and transferred to Venus it produces the first prediction of the surface muon flux, an environment for which no measurement exists. The agent thus extends the workflow from auditable reproduction to first-principles prediction: it autonomously reconfigures the simulation(atmosphere, magnetic field, electric field)for new environments, while the proton-only primary model, limited high-momentum statistics, and an incomplete systematic-uncertainty treatment bound the physical precision that can currently be claimed.

papers.title_en: Measurements of lepton-flavour universality in semileptonic $B$ decays at Belle and Belle II
papers.abstract_en: Tests of lepton-flavour universality in semileptonic \(B\)-meson decays provide sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model. The Belle and Belle II experiments, respectively operating on the KEKB and SuperKEKB colliders in Japan, have collected \(e^+e^-\to B\bar{B}\) collisions at a center-of-mass energy corresponding to the \(Υ(4S)\) resonance in samples with a combined integrated luminosity exceeding \(1\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}\). These data, with low particle multiplicity, constrained initial-state kinematics, and excellent lepton identification, provide an ideal environment to study lepton-flavour universality in semileptonic decays of \(B\) mesons. New results on the ratios of semitauonic \(B\)-decay rates compared to analogous light-lepton rates are presented. These include new Belle II measurements of branching-fraction ratios \(R(D^{(*)})\) involving exclusive \(B\to D^{(*)}τν\) and \(B\to D^{(*)}\ellν\) decays using semileptonic or hadronic reconstruction of the accompanying \(B\)-meson tag. Belle II and Belle measurements of angular observables in \(B\to D^*\ellν\) modes that test light-lepton universality and the Lorentz structure of the decay are also presented. The measurements are statistically limited and individually consistent with Standard Model expectations. The new \(R(D^{(*)})\) results are also compatible with experimental world averages, which continue to exhibit tension with Standard Model predictions. Belle II has now accumulated an \(Υ(4S)\) data sample exceeding that of Belle, offering substantial opportunities for new analysis approaches and heightened precision.

papers.title_en: Quantum state texture of maximal-resource Fourier states under Hawking radiation
papers.abstract_en: Quantum state texture (QST) is a recently proposed quantum resource that characterizes the nonuniformity of a density matrix in a given computational basis. In the resource theory of QST, the Fourier states f_k are maximally resourceful states, attaining the maximum QST measure. We study the QST behavior of three maximally resourceful states in a two-mode Dirac field under Hawking radiation from a Schwarzschild black hole, using a fidelity-based measure. We consider three cases: only mode B undergoes radiation, only mode A undergoes radiation, and both modes undergo radiation simultaneously. Our results show that for single-mode radiation, if the mode unaffected by radiation is orthogonal to the single-mode textureless state, the QST of the overall output state remains maximal and is independent of the Hawking temperature; we call this phenomenon orthogonality protection. When both modes undergo radiation simultaneously, orthogonality protection vanishes, and the QST of all three Fourier states decreases with increasing Hawking temperature. Notably, the QST measure of f_3 under two-mode radiation is higher than that under only mode B radiation, indicating that QST can be redistributed among modes: QST gained by one mode under radiation can partially compensate for QST lost by the other. We further provide a general resource-theoretic explanation of orthogonality protection, showing that this phenomenon is independent of the specific form of the QST measure. These results reveal how QST degrades under Hawking radiation and provide a new perspective on the redistribution of quantum resources in black hole backgrounds.

papers.title_en: Towards the Geometry of Quantum Optical Measurements: Kraus Trajectories in the Instrumental Weyl-Heisenberg Group Manifold
papers.abstract_en: Since ancient Greek times, geometry has been a method by which humans can make inferences, by the use of similar triangles, about the world far beyond their immediate senses. Similarity plays an equally important role in quantum measurement, except that instead of triangles, the similarity is between the infinitesimal generators of rotation, canonical transformation, or some other virtual symmetry. For many quantum optical measurements of a single mode, these generators produce Kraus operators that are contained within a twelve-dimensional Lie group: the Instrumental Weyl-Heisenberg group manifold ($\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$). In particular, $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ is general enough to include all diffusively generated 'dyne measurements. In this paper, $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ will be used to develop two more general classes of 'dyne measurement: one that interpolates between diffusive homodyne and diffusive heterodyne (``slomodyne'') and one that adds to 'dyne measurements adaptive squeezing and displacement. Our analysis uses an approach known as the Instrument Manifold Program (IMP). In particular, a Harish-Chandra-like decomposition of $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ is used to calculate the vielbein transformation from a right-invariant basis to the corresponding coordinate basis, allowing us to universally and autonomously navigate $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ and locate the Kraus-operator of whatever selective process is being considered as it evolves in time according to the measurement record.

papers.title_en: Bosonic Quantum Conditional Mutual Information and Bose-Einstein Condensation
papers.abstract_en: This article aims to introduce the bosonic asymmetric quantum conditional mutual information (QCMI), $I_{B}(A; B|C)$, as a rigorously defined information-theoretic quantity for continuous-variable (bosonic) systems. After defining $I_{B}(A; B|C)$ through quantum instruments on infinite-dimensional Fock spaces, we prove that Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) induces a logarithmic divergence $ I_{B}(A; B|C) \geq α\log_2 (N_{0}^C+1)$, which further establishes $I_{B}(A; B|C)$ as a quantum-information order parameter for BEC with power-law scaling near the critical point. We provide the complete five-step proof of this result, connecting measurement back-action, off-diagonal long-range order, and Jensen's inequality. In the condensed phase, the effective causal propagation velocity is set by the Bogoliubov sound speed $c_s$ in the long-wavelength limit, and vanishes continuously at the superfluid--Mott-insulator transition. Applications to composite bosons, the BEC--BCS crossover, and a quantum-gas-microscope measurement protocol are presented. Finally, we demonstrate how the reduced bosonic QCMI serves as a finite-size scaling probe analogous to the Binder cumulant.

papers.title_en: The Thousand-Pulsar-Array programme on MeerKAT - XX. Co-existing interacting periodicities and polarization modulation in PSR J1901-0906
papers.abstract_en: We present a comprehensive analysis of the complex subpulse modulation in PSR J1901-0906 using data from the Thousand-Pulsar-Array (TPA) programme. Our analysis reveals the coexistence of three distinct periodicities in the subpulse modulation of both profile components, which obey a beat relation. We also detect additional spectral beat features caused by the modulation of these co-existing periodicities by investigating the Fourier phase correlation in two-dimensional fluctuation spectra. Moreover, the single-pulse polarization states are shown to be modulated and synchronized with the three co-existing periodicities observed in total intensity. Such synchronization has been reported for only a small number of pulsars, but this discovery marks the only one where this synchronization involves multiple co-existing periodicities. The modulation beats are similar to, yet more complex than, the beat system previously identified in PSR J1514-4834 with higher-order harmonics playing a significant role. The coexistence of the observed beat-like periodicities in PSR J1901-0906 implies that they are not independent, but rather originate from an underlying, interconnected physical system within the pulsar magnetosphere. Building upon the same geometric framework previously applied to PSR J1514-4834, we demonstrate that a feedback system with interacting rotating carousels successfully reproduces the complex subpulse modulations observed in PSR J1901-0906 and naturally explains the beat relations.

papers.title_en: Deterministic positioning accuracy of B centers in hBN by electron irradiation
papers.abstract_en: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is a promising material platform for quantum technologies, enabling both the realization of nanophotonic devices and the hosting of point defects that act as high-quality single-photon emitters (SPEs). Among these defects, B centers, which reproducibly emit at 436 nm, can be generated individually at predefined positions using electron beam irradiation, a crucial capability for top-down quantum photonics. Yet, the spatial accuracy of emitter creation strongly conditions the potential applications. Here, we generate arrays of individual B centers in a scanning electron microscope (SEM) with in-situ cathodoluminescence (CL) monitoring. We characterize the sources of random deviations from the target positions to identify the limitations to their deterministic positioning. In particular, we measure the distance between the electron beam and the emitter at the moment the emitter is created based on CL mapping. This approach provides a direct estimation of the spatial extent of the beam-emitter interaction. We find this contribution to be the main constraint to the emitter fabrication accuracy, yielding a standard deviation of 27 nm. Additional contributions, primarily from the finite density of UV-emitting carbon dimer precursors, increase the overall positional standard deviation to 40 nm. Our results highlight the possible improvements to the B center creation technique to reach sub-10 nm accuracy.

papers.title_en: Concurrence Dynamics in Self-Gravitating Mixed Neutrinos
papers.abstract_en: We study the entanglement generated by Newtonian self-gravity in a two-particle system of mixed neutrinos and quantify it by means of the concurrence. Starting from the gravitational coupling between the mass operators, we show that the two-particle Hamiltonian splits into local single-particle terms and an effective Ising interaction in the mass basis, the latter being solely responsible for the generation of correlations. For initially separable flavor states the concurrence is obtained in closed analytic form: it oscillates between zero and a maximum fixed by the mixing angle alone, while the gravitational coupling sets the recurrence time. We further establish a one-to-one correspondence between the concurrence and the reduced-state purity previously derived for this model, thus providing an independent quantum-information description of the same gravitationally induced correlations. Finally, we show that the concurrence does not depend on the Majorana phase, so that Dirac and Majorana parametrizations yield identical entanglement dynamics. These results isolate the genuinely entangling sector of the gravitational evolution and provide a compact analytic characterization of gravity-induced quantum correlations in mixed neutrino systems.

papers.title_en: About P-adic Numbers and Professor Igor Volovich on the Occasion of his 80th Anniversary
papers.abstract_en: We recall a 1987 paper written by Volovich and our subsequent work with Okada which established the Feyman rules for the p-adic string and the related non-local field theory which found diverse physical applications. We add some memories of visits to Moscow during 1989-91.

papers.title_en: Readout chain of SPD DAQ system
papers.abstract_en: The Spin Physics Detector (SPD) experiment at the NICA collider of the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research (JINR) aims to study the spin structure of the nucleon and spin-related phenomena. The experimental conditions, including the high interaction rate and the large number of readout channels, require a triggerless data acquisition system with high throughput and a scalable architecture. This work presents a hardware implementation of the readout chain that extends the previously proposed SPD DAQ architecture. The chain is based on two levels of concentrators. The L1 concentrator provides the interface between the front-end electronics and the next system level and distributes synchronous signals. The L2 concentrator aggregates data streams from several L1 concentrators before transmitting them to the computing system. A key feature of the L2 implementation is the offloading of data reception, buffering, and aggregation from the host CPU to the FPGA, motivated by the large number of small packets generated by the readout electronics. The developed hardware platforms and their operating logic are presented, together with experimental results for the main interfaces and data-path components. The obtained results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed hardware architecture and its application in a scalable SPD data acquisition system.
